```{r}
#| label: fig-tepr-timecourse
#| fig-cap: "Task-Evoked Pupil Response (TEPR) Time Course. Grand-average pupil traces (baseline-corrected, mean ± 95% CI) aligned to squeeze onset for four conditions (Easy/Low, Easy/High, Hard/Low, Hard/High), separately for ADT (top) and VDT (bottom). The shaded region indicates the cognitive AUC window used for TEPR quantification (4.65s to 7.65s relative to squeeze onset, extending from 300ms after target stimulus onset until ~3s post-target). Baseline-corrected traces converge at 0 during the baseline period (-0.5 to 0s). Vertical dashed lines indicate key events: trial start (0s), target stimulus onset (4.35s), and response signal onset (4.7s)."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "85%"
#| echo: false
# Generate TEPR time course figure
if (!is.null(pupil_data)) {
  # Try to load waveform summary data
  waveform_file <- file.path(proj_root, "quick_share_v7/analysis/pupil_waveforms_condition_mean.csv")
  
  if (file.exists(waveform_file)) {
    waveform_data <- read_csv(waveform_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
    
    # Filter to chapter 3 data and keep all 4 conditions (effort × difficulty)
    waveform_ch3 <- waveform_data %>%
      filter(chapter == "ch3") %>%
      # Map difficulty level from stimulus_intensity and isOddball
      mutate(
        difficulty_level = case_when(
          isOddball == 0 | (is.na(isOddball) & (!is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity == 0)) ~ "Standard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Hard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(3, 4) ~ "Easy",
          isOddball == 1 & is.na(stimulus_intensity) ~ "Easy",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        effort_level = case_when(
          effort == "Low" | effort == "Low_Force_5pct" ~ "Low",
          effort == "High" | effort == "High_Force_40pct" ~ "High",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        # Create condition label (Difficulty / Effort)
        condition = case_when(
          !is.na(difficulty_level) & !is.na(effort_level) ~ 
            paste0(difficulty_level, " / ", effort_level),
          TRUE ~ "Unknown"
        )
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        difficulty_level = gsub("\u2013", "-", difficulty_level),
        effort_level = gsub("\u2013", "-", effort_level),
        condition = gsub("\u2013", "-", condition)
      ) %>%
      # Filter out Standard trials (we want Easy/Hard only) and Unknown
      filter(condition != "Unknown", !grepl("Standard", condition)) %>%
      # Use mean_pupil_full (baseline-corrected, B0-corrected) - this converges at 0 in baseline period
      # Per plot_pupil_waveforms.R line 134: mean_pupil_full is the B0-corrected (full baseline correction)
      rename(mean_pupil_isolated = mean_pupil_full) %>%
      # Group by task, condition, and time to get per-condition means
      group_by(task, condition, t_rel) %>%
      summarise(
        # Weighted mean across any duplicate entries (weight by n_trials)
        total_trials = sum(n_trials, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_pupil_isolated = sum(mean_pupil_isolated * n_trials, na.rm = TRUE) / total_trials,
        n_trials = total_trials,
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(task), !is.na(condition), !is.na(t_rel), !is.na(mean_pupil_isolated)) %>%
      arrange(task, condition, t_rel)
    
    if (nrow(waveform_ch3) > 0) {
      # Define event markers and cognitive AUC window
      # Based on Methods section: cognitive AUC window is 4.65s to 7.65s (300ms after target until 3.3s post-target)
      trial_start <- 0.0  # Trial start (squeeze onset)
      target_onset <- 4.35  # Target stimulus onset
      response_signal_onset <- 4.7  # Response signal onset
      cognitive_auc_start <- 4.65  # 300ms after target onset (4.35 + 0.3)
      cognitive_auc_end <- 7.65  # 3.3s post-target (4.35 + 3.3), which is the Decision-Phase AUC (W3.0) window
      
      # Define color scheme for 4 conditions (matching plot_pupil_waveforms.R)
      condition_colors <- c(
        "Easy / Low" = "#5DADE2",    # Light blue
        "Easy / High" = "#2E86AB",   # Dark blue  
        "Hard / Low" = "#EC70AB",    # Light pink
        "Hard / High" = "#A23B72"    # Dark pink
      )
      
      # Get conditions actually present in data
      conditions_present <- unique(waveform_ch3$condition)
      conditions_present <- conditions_present[!is.na(conditions_present)]
      colors_for_plot <- condition_colors[names(condition_colors) %in% conditions_present]
      if (length(colors_for_plot) == 0) {
        # Fallback: use default colors if no matches
        colors_for_plot <- scales::hue_pal()(length(conditions_present))
        names(colors_for_plot) <- conditions_present
      }
      
      # Calculate y-limits from data (use full range to show all curves, add padding for labels)
      y_vals <- waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated[!is.na(waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated)]
      if (length(y_vals) > 0) {
        # Use full range to ensure all curves are visible
        y_range <- range(y_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
        y_range_span <- diff(y_range)
        if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) {
          y_range_span <- max(abs(y_range), na.rm = TRUE)
          if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) y_range_span <- 1
        }
        # Add padding (12% top, 8% bottom) to accommodate labels and ensure visibility
        y_upper_limit <- y_range[2] + y_range_span * 0.12  # Extra space for labels
        y_lower_limit <- y_range[1] - y_range_span * 0.08  # Padding at bottom
      } else {
        y_upper_limit <- 0.5
        y_lower_limit <- -0.5
        y_range_span <- 1  # Default span for label positioning
      }
      
      # Event markers with staggered y positions to avoid overlap (vertical text)
      event_markers <- tibble(
        event = c("Trial Start", "Target", "Response"),
        time = c(trial_start, target_onset, response_signal_onset),
        label_y = y_upper_limit - y_range_span * c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15)  # Stagger vertically
      )
      
      # Create plot
      p_tepr <- ggplot(waveform_ch3, aes(x = t_rel, y = mean_pupil_isolated, 
                                         color = condition, fill = condition)) +
        # Cognitive AUC window shading
        geom_rect(aes(xmin = cognitive_auc_start, xmax = cognitive_auc_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.3) +
        # GAM smoothed lines with confidence intervals
        geom_smooth(se = TRUE, method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 20), 
                    linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.3) +
        # Event markers (vertical dashed lines)
        geom_vline(data = event_markers, aes(xintercept = time), 
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
        # Event labels (vertical text to avoid overlap)
        geom_text(data = event_markers, aes(x = time, y = label_y, label = event),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.9,
                  size = 3.5, color = "grey20", fontface = "bold") +
        # Facet by task (stacked vertically)
        facet_wrap(~task, ncol = 1, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", 
                                                                  "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
        # Scales
        scale_color_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 8, 1), expand = c(0, 0.1)) +
        coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_lower_limit, y_upper_limit)) +
        # Labels and theme
        labs(
          x = "Time (s, relative to squeeze onset)",
          y = "Baseline-Corrected Pupil Diameter (AU)",
          title = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.5),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
        )
      
      # Print plot
      print(p_tepr)
    } else {
      # Placeholder if no data
      # Waveform data not available - ensure label still resolves
      invisible(NULL)
    }
  } else {
    # Placeholder if file not found
    # Waveform file not found - ensure label still resolves
    invisible(NULL)
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder if pupil_data not loaded - use invisible output to ensure label resolves
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

### Key Contrasts: Hypothesis Tests {#sec-key-contrasts}

To evaluate our a priori predictions about how effort and difficulty modulate decision parameters, we examined posterior contrasts on the link scale.

Contrasts on the link scale confirmed large effects of difficulty on drift rate ($v$), with Easy $>$ Hard $>$ Standard, and consistent effects of effort on $v$. Boundary separation ($a$) and starting-point bias ($z$) showed more modest modulation by difficulty and effort.

**Bayesian inference as hypothesis testing.** In a hierarchical Bayesian framework, inference proceeds via **posterior contrasts** — the full posterior distribution of the difference between two conditions, extracted from the fitted model [@burkner2017brms; @ratcliff2008diffusion]. For each hypothesis, we compute $\delta = \hat{\theta}_\text{High} - \hat{\theta}_\text{Low}$ from the posterior draws and report (1) the posterior median of $\delta$, (2) a 95% credible interval (or Highest Density Interval, HDI, where appropriate), and (3) the posterior probability $P(\delta < 0)$ — the proportion of posterior mass below zero, which summarizes how strongly the data support a negative effort effect when that is the directional prediction. When a 95% CrI excludes zero, essentially all posterior mass lies on the predicted side of zero, which is the Bayesian sense in which the evidence is decisive for that directional claim. **This goes beyond a point-estimate test** because it quantifies *how much* of the posterior mass aligns with the prediction, not only where the median lands. The posterior distributions of all key contrasts are visualized in @fig-effort-drift-posterior-diff and @fig-difficulty-contrasts, which serve as the primary inferential figures for H1–H4.

Relative to the hypotheses in Section 1.4.1: Consistent with H1, High effort (40% MVC) produced reliably lower drift rates than Low effort (5% MVC; `r h1_beta_str`, `r h1_cri_str``r h1_p0_str`), with the 95% credible interval excluding zero — evidence that concurrent grip maintenance degraded the quality of evidence accumulation. For H2, the boundary-separation effort contrast was concentrated near zero with the credible interval spanning zero (`r h2_beta_str`, `r h2_cri_str``r h2_null_note`): `r h2_evidence_label` (auxiliary ROPE mass `r h2_p_in_rope_pct`; see @tbl-hyp-summary). H3 (non-decision time) could not be directly tested in the primary model: $t_0$ was constrained to an intercept-only specification for stability in the response-signal design (@sec-ddm-spec and Section 3.5). An exploratory effort contrast (`r h3_beta_str`, `r h3_cri_str`; `r h3_natural`) should not be treated as firm evidence of absence of a non-decision-time effect. For H4, the starting-point bias effort contrast was likewise near zero and uncertain (`r h4_beta_str`, `r h4_cri_str``r h4_p0_str`): `r h4_evidence_label` (auxiliary ROPE mass `r h4_p_in_rope_pct`). A robust task difference was observed, however: ADT showed a reliably stronger bias toward *different* responses than VDT (`r h4task_beta_str`, `r h4task_cri_str``r h4task_p0_str`), a contrast that clearly excluded zero. The standard-only calibration estimates, which provide the cleanest measure of pre-stimulus bias free from drift-rate confounding, are reported in Section 3.5 and Appendix A2.

#### Distinguishing Near-Zero, Design-Limited, and Inconclusive Effects {#sec-null-inference}

Not all non-supported hypotheses carry equal inferential weight, and treating them uniformly risks misleading readers about the strength of evidence. This chapter distinguishes four categories. First, H1 is **supported**: the posterior is entirely consistent with a negative effort effect on drift rate, and the credible interval excludes zero. Second, H2 (boundary separation) and H4 (starting-point bias) produced posteriors concentrated near zero whose 95% CrIs span zero — these represent **near-zero** patterns in that the data are consistent with at most a small effect; **auxiliary** project-convention ROPE summaries (±0.05 on the log and logit link scales for $a$ and $z$; pipeline-derived, not a pre-registered SESOI) provide a secondary description of posterior concentration but **do not constitute formal equivalence testing**. Third, H3 (non-decision time) is **not directly testable** in the primary model: the response-signal paradigm required constraining $t_0$ to an intercept-only specification for model stability; any exploratory effort effect on $\log t_0$ is therefore a descriptive supplement, not a valid H3 test. Fourth, all pupil-linked predictors are **inconclusive due to measurement and model-comparison limitations**: the trial-wise TEPR window (Decision-Phase AUC) likely conflates motor-autonomic and cognitive dilation under sustained grip, and PSIS-LOO model comparison was unreliable (max Pareto-$k$ = 0.91). @tbl-hyp-summary tabulates all nine primary effects in this framework. **ROPE mass** in that table is an auxiliary project-level sensitivity summary (footnote [b]); it does not replace CrI-based inference and is not a preregistered or externally anchored equivalence test.

```{r}

P(in ROPE): auxiliary project-convention thresholds ($\\pm$0.05 log/logit; $\\pm$0.02 identity link); not formal equivalence testing (see footnote [b]). n/a = not applicable for design-constrained or measurement-limited effects. Conditional-slope estimates for TEPR $\\times$ difficulty appear in @tbl-pupil-key-effects. Note a: H3 $t_0$ fixed to intercept-only (response-signal design); exploratory estimate only. We next examine starting-point bias in isolation through a standard-only calibration model that separates bias from drift rate.

### Task Modality Effects {#sec-task-modality}

Sensitivity analyses confirmed that the Effort → Drift effect was robust to Task inclusion (Appendix~A4.3). Although auditory and visual tasks differed in absolute drift rates (Task main effect $\beta \approx 0.07$, 95% CrI [0.02, 0.12]), the Effort × Task interaction was negligible and its 95% CrI included zero ($\beta \approx 0.03$, 95% CrI [−0.03, 0.09]), indicating that High effort reduced drift rate similarly in both modalities. @fig-suppl-drift-by-task and @fig-suppl-boundary-by-task (Appendix~A4.3) show drift rate and boundary separation estimates separately for ADT and VDT across all difficulty and effort conditions. The difficulty gradient (Standard $<$ Hard $<$ Easy) is consistent across both modalities, with VDT showing slightly lower absolute drift rates than ADT. Difficulty strongly modulates caution (Easy $<$ Standard $<$ Hard) in both tasks; effort contrasts on boundary separation are near-zero in both modalities (discussed in Section 3.5.2), providing no evidence of task-specific boundary adjustment under increased physical effort.

Full statistical results including parameter estimates and contrasts are reported in Appendix~A4.3, Table 22. <!-- FIXED: Table 23 is pupil-LOO; primary DDM contrasts are in Table 22 per Report-3 audit -->

## Starting-Point Bias and H4: Standard-Only Calibration

In a separate calibration model fit to Standard trials only, starting-point bias ($z$) was estimated independently of drift rate ($v$). Bias values were consistently above 0.5, indicating a systematic tendency toward "different" responses. The task contrast was robust: VDT showed reliably *lower* bias toward "different" responses than ADT ($\Delta z = -0.04$, 95% CrI [−0.06, −0.02], a contrast excluding zero; @tbl-standard-only-bias-contrasts, @fig-bias-by-task). By contrast, the effort contrast was small and uncertain (Low−High: `r h4_beta_str`, `r h4_cri_str``r h4_p0_str`; credible interval spans zero), providing no credible evidence that grip force at 40% MVC shifted pre-stimulus response tendencies — though the interval width alone does not constitute a formal proof of no effect. To contextualise the magnitude: the effort contrast corresponds to approximately `r h4_effort_vs_task_str`, and represents a shift of less than two percentage points on the 0–1 response-probability scale.

```{r drift-standard-compute}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute drift rate on Standard trials for inline use
v_standard <- -1.1
if (!is.null(pred_params) && nrow(pred_params) > 0) {
  v_std_data <- pred_params %>%
    filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR, difficulty == "Standard")
  if (nrow(v_std_data) > 0) {
    v_standard <- round(mean(v_std_data$drift_median, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  }
}
```

Starting-point bias ($z$) represents the participant's pre-stimulus expectation before any sensory information is gathered. Crucially, as specified in our hierarchical model (`z ~ task + effort`), bias was estimated independently of trial difficulty because participants did not know whether an upcoming trial would be Standard, Easy, or Hard. Therefore, the estimated bias reflects a global task strategy rather than a trial-specific reaction. Across tasks, older adults exhibited a systematic pre-stimulus bias toward the "Different" boundary ($z > 0.5$). In Signal Detection Theory terms, this reflects a **liberal** detection criterion — participants were predisposed to report "Different" with relatively low evidentiary thresholds, not a conservative one. This pattern is consistent with the "Different-as-default heuristic" documented in same-different paradigms [@farell1985; @nosofsky1997palmeri], discussed further in relation to boundary separation in Section 3.5.1. By adopting a starting point biased toward the "Different" boundary, older adults reduced the cognitive demands of Standard (Same) trials — at the cost of elevated false alarm rates on trials where stimuli were in fact identical.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-standard-only-bias-contrasts
#| tbl-cap: "Standard-only bias contrasts (posterior differences in $z$; $p_{>0} = P(\\Delta z > 0)$). Includes both task contrast (Visual − Auditory) and effort contrast (Low − High)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build bias contrasts table with dissertation-grade validation (using standardized column names)
tbl_bias_contr_raw <- std_bias_contrasts %>%
  filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT)

# DISSERTATION-GRADE VALIDATION: Stop if any CI columns are missing
if (anyNA(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q2.5) || anyNA(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q97.5)) {
  missing_q2.5 <- sum(is.na(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q2.5))
  missing_q97.5 <- sum(is.na(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q97.5))

    filter(is.na(q2.5) | is.na(q97.5)) %>%
    select(contrast, estimate, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0)
  
  stop("standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv has NA credible intervals. Re-run postprocess step.\n",
       "  Missing q2.5: ", missing_q2.5, " rows\n",
       "  Missing q97.5: ", missing_q97.5, " rows\n",
       "  Broken rows:\n",
       paste(capture.output(print(broken_rows)), collapse = "\n"),
       call. = FALSE)
}

# Build display table - include ALL contrasts (no filtering; use manuscript-ready labels)
tbl_bias_contr <- tbl_bias_contr_raw %>%
  select(contrast, estimate, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0) %>%
  mutate(
    contrast = format_contrast_display(contrast),
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    q2.5 = round(q2.5, 3),
    q97.5 = round(q97.5, 3),
    p_gt0 = dplyr::case_when(
      round(p_gt0, 3) >= 0.999 ~ "> .999",

    `Contrast` = contrast,

    `P(Δz > 0)` = p_gt0
  )

message(sprintf("Bias contrasts table: %d rows (should include both Task and Effort contrasts)", nrow(tbl_bias_contr)))

tbl_bias_contr %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"),

### Integrated Condition Effects

To summarize how difficulty and effort jointly influenced all DDM parameters, @fig-integrated-condition-effects shows integrated condition effects on $v$, $a$, and $z$. Difficulty effects were strongest for boundary separation ($a$), with Easy trials showing reduced caution relative to Hard trials. The structural asymmetry in boundary separation and reaction time distributions between "Standard" (Same) and "Easy/Hard" (Different) trials is driven by underlying cognitive search mechanisms. Identifying a mismatch in an Easy or Hard trial allows for a **self-terminating search**—the moment a disparate feature is detected, evidence accumulation spikes, triggering a fast, confident response. Conversely, confirming that two complex stimuli are identical in a Standard trial requires an **exhaustive search** of all features. This exhaustive process is inherently slower and demands a wider boundary separation ($a$) to guard against false alarms, explaining why the parameter profiles for the "Standard" condition fundamentally differ from the detection conditions. <!-- FIXED: t0 claim contradicted model spec; replaced with constraint statement per Report-3 audit --> Non-decision time ($t_0$) was constrained to be constant across all conditions ($t_0 = 0.347$ s) for model stability in the response-signal design (see Section 2.3.2); condition-specific $t_0$ variation is therefore not interpretable from the primary model. Bias ($z$) varied by task and effort but not by difficulty, consistent with the design constraints described in the Methods.

```{r}
#| label: fig-integrated-condition-effects
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| fig-cap: "Integrated condition effects on DDM parameters $v$, $a$, and $z$. Multi-panel forest plot showing posterior means with 95% credible intervals for difficulty and effort effects on drift rate ($v$), boundary separation ($a$), and starting-point bias ($z$). Bias ($z$) does not vary by difficulty (see Methods). *Note: Drift rates ($v$) were estimated using Response Coding. Positive values indicate evidence accumulation toward the 'Different' boundary; negative values indicate accumulation toward the 'Same' boundary.*"
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "70%"
#| fig-height: 10
# Dynamic: from fixef_link (run_dir)
if (!is.null(fixef_link) && nrow(fixef_link) > 0) {
  fx_int <- fixef_link %>%
    filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT) %>%
    filter(!grepl("^ndt_", term), term != "Intercept", !grepl("^bs_Intercept$|^bias_Intercept$", term)) %>%
    mutate(
      param_type = case_when(
        grepl("^bs_", term) ~ "Boundary (a)",
        grepl("^bias_", term) ~ "Bias (z)",
        grepl("^b_", term) | (!grepl("^bs_|^bias_", term) & grepl("Intercept", term)) ~ "Drift (v)",
        TRUE ~ "Drift (v)"
      ),
      term_clean = case_when(
        grepl("difficulty_3Hard", term) ~ "Hard vs Standard",
        grepl("difficulty_3Easy", term) ~ "Easy vs Standard",
        grepl("effort_conditionhigh", term) ~ "High vs Low",
        grepl("taskVDT", term) ~ "VDT vs ADT",
        TRUE ~ gsub("difficulty_3|effort_condition|bias_|bs_", "", term)
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(term_clean %in% c("Hard vs Standard", "Easy vs Standard", "High vs Low", "VDT vs ADT"))
  if (nrow(fx_int) > 0) {
    p_int <- ggplot(fx_int, aes(x = Estimate, y = term_clean)) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60", linewidth = 0.5) +
      geom_point(aes(color = param_type), size = 1.5) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Q2.5, xmax = Q97.5, color = param_type), height = 0.15, linewidth = 0.6) +
      facet_wrap(~ param_type, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Drift (v)" = "#2E86AB", "Boundary (a)" = "#A23B72", "Bias (z)" = "#28A745")) +
      labs(title = "Integrated Condition Effects on DDM Parameters",
           subtitle = "Posterior means with 95% credible intervals (link scale). Effort effect on drift rate is consistent across ADT and VDT (non-significant Effort \u00d7 Task interaction; see Section 3.4.2).",
           x = "Effect Estimate (95% CrI)", y = "Condition", color = "Parameter") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray60"),
            strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10), legend.position = "bottom",
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
    print(p_int)
  } else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_integrated_condition_effects.pdf"))
  }
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_integrated_condition_effects.pdf"))
}

### Individual Differences

```{r cor-val-setup}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute cor_val_fig17 here (before inline reference) so caption and text agree.
cor_val_fig17 <- -0.205  # fallback
model_path_cor_early <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "models",
                                  "additive__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds")
if (file.exists(model_path_cor_early) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tryCatch({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(brms))
    fit_cor_e <- readRDS(model_path_cor_early)
    coef_e    <- brms::coef(fit_cor_e, summary = TRUE)
    if (!is.null(coef_e) && "subject_id" %in% names(coef_e)) {
      d_e <- coef_e$subject_id[, , "Intercept"]
      b_e <- coef_e$subject_id[, , "bias_Intercept"]
      if (!is.null(d_e) && !is.null(b_e))
        cor_val_fig17 <- cor(d_e[, "Estimate"], b_e[, "Estimate"], use = "complete.obs")
    }
  }, error = function(e) invisible(NULL))
}
# Build caption for fig-parameter-correlation (used in chunk option)
fig17_cap <- sprintf(
  "Subject-Level Parameter Correlation: Drift Intercept vs. Bias Intercept. Scatter plot showing the relationship between subject-level random-effect estimates for drift intercept and bias intercept. Each point represents one participant (n = 67). The correlation is r = %.3f, indicating a %s association; participants with stronger negative drift tend to show %s starting-point bias. The regression line with 95%% confidence band is shown.",
  cor_val_fig17,
  ifelse(abs(cor_val_fig17) < 0.3, "weak", ifelse(abs(cor_val_fig17) < 0.6, "moderate", "strong")),
  ifelse(cor_val_fig17 < 0, "slightly lower", "slightly higher")

```

The hierarchical structure revealed substantial individual differences in all DDM parameters, with drift rate showing the widest variability. Parameter correlations revealed a weak negative relationship ($r$ = `r sprintf("%.3f", cor_val_fig17)`) between drift intercept and bias intercept at the subject level. Supporting figures are provided in Appendix~A2 (@fig-subject-parameter-distribution and @fig-brinley-plot).

**Divergence between standard-only and primary model bias estimates.** The starting-point bias estimate from the standard-only calibration model ($z = 0.63$, 95% CrI [0.60, 0.66]; @tbl-standard-only-bias-levels) is notably higher than the estimates from the primary model fit to all trials ($z \approx 0.52$–$0.55$ across conditions; @tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort). This divergence is an expected consequence of model structure, not an inconsistency.

In the primary model, starting-point bias $z$ is estimated jointly with drift rate $v$ across Standard, Hard, and Easy trials. Because Standard and Hard trials have strongly negative drift rates ($v \approx -0.50$ to $-1.09$; @tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort) — reflecting that participants frequently give "Different" responses on these difficult same-match trials — the model faces competition between attributing this response pattern to (a) low bias toward "Different" with strong negative drift, or (b) high bias toward "Different" with weaker negative drift. This trade-off applies subtle downward pressure on the bias estimate in the joint model.

In contrast, the standard-only model isolates bias by fitting only Standard ($\Delta = 0$) trials, where drift rate is theoretically zero and cannot explain response tendencies. This removes the $v$–$z$ trade-off, yielding a purer estimate of the pre-stimulus starting-point preference. For interpretive purposes, we treat the standard-only estimate ($z = 0.63$) as the canonical measure of response bias, as it most directly reflects participants' a priori tendency to favor the "Different" response independent of evidence accumulation dynamics. The lower estimate from the primary model ($z \approx 0.52$–$0.55$) represents the effective bias after accounting for the joint contribution of drift and starting point to the full response pattern.

Having established that the behavioral DDM adequately captures the key parameter patterns, we turn to the pupil-linked extension, which tests whether trial-wise phasic arousal further modulates evidence accumulation or response bias.

## Pupil-linked modulation of decision parameters {#sec-pupil-ddm-integration}

To examine whether trial-wise arousal fluctuations modulate decision parameters, we compared a nested sequence of four pupil-augmented DDM specifications (see @sec-pupil-ddm-models): (1) a **behavioral baseline** model with no pupil predictor; (2) a **pupil → bias** model, testing whether TEPR predicts starting-point bias $z$ — directly relevant to H4 (bias neutrality under arousal); (3) a **pupil → drift + bias** model, testing whether TEPR also modulates drift rate $v$ — an exploratory extension of the phasic arousal–evidence accumulation hypothesis; and (4) a **pupil × Difficulty** interaction model, testing the Yerkes–Dodson prediction that arousal effects on $v$ should diverge across difficulty levels. Models were compared with PSIS-LOO relative to the behavioral baseline on the pupil-available trial subset. **Pareto-$k$ diagnostics exceeded 0.7 for all pupil-augmented models (max $k = 0.91$), so ELPD differences are not a reliable basis for model selection** [@vehtari2017loo]; we therefore treat apparent $\Delta$ELPD values as descriptive at most and **interpret pupil effects primarily from posterior coefficients** (@tbl-pupil-key-effects, below). In that light, pooled TEPR coefficients were centered near zero with CrIs spanning zero (reported below).

Table 8 summarizes trial-evoked pupil response (TEPR) magnitude by Difficulty and Effort condition, providing descriptive context for the pupil predictor entered into the models reported below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tepr
#| tbl-cap: "Task-Evoked Pupil Response (TEPR) by Condition"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Compute TEPR (cognitive AUC) by task, difficulty, and effort
if (!is.null(pupil_data) && "cognitive_auc" %in% names(pupil_data) && "task" %in% names(pupil_data) && "effort_condition" %in% names(pupil_data) && "difficulty_level" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
  tepr_summary <- pupil_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(cognitive_auc), !is.na(task), !is.na(effort_condition), !is.na(difficulty_level)) %>%
    group_by(task, difficulty_level, effort_condition, subject_id) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_cog_auc = mean(cognitive_auc, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(task, difficulty_level, effort_condition) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_auc = round(mean(mean_cog_auc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      sd_auc = round(sd(mean_cog_auc, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      n_subjects = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = case_when(
        task == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
        task == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
        TRUE ~ task
      ),
      Difficulty = case_when(
        difficulty_level == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
        difficulty_level == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
        difficulty_level == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
        TRUE ~ difficulty_level
      ),
      Effort = case_when(
        effort_condition == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
        effort_condition == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
        TRUE ~ effort_condition
      ),
      `Mean AUC` = mean_auc,
      `SD AUC` = sd_auc,
      `N Subjects` = n_subjects
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = gsub("\u2013", "-", Task_Group),
      Difficulty = gsub("\u2013", "-", Difficulty),
      Effort = gsub("\u2013", "-", Effort)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort) %>%
    select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, `Mean AUC`, `SD AUC`, `N Subjects`)
  
  # Note: Peak amplitude calculation would require time-series data
  # For now, we report AUC as the primary TEPR metric
  tepr_summary %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(`Mean AUC`, `SD AUC`), decimals = 3) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = `N Subjects`, decimals = 0) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
      locations = cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      row_group.as_column = FALSE,
      row_group.padding = px(8)
    ) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "TEPR (phasic arousal) quantified as Cognitive AUC (Area Under the Curve) from baseline-corrected pupil data using the Decision-Phase AUC (W3.0) window (4.65s to 7.65s, target+0.3s to target+3.3s). AUC in units of AU·s.",
      locations = cells_column_labels(columns = `Mean AUC`)
    )
} else {
  # Placeholder if data not available
  tepr_placeholder <- expand_grid(
    task = c("ADT", "VDT"),
    difficulty_level = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard"),
    effort_condition = c("Low_5_MVC", "High_40_MVC")
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = case_when(
        task == "ADT" ~ "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)",
        task == "VDT" ~ "VDT (Visual Detection Task)",
        TRUE ~ task
      ),
      Difficulty = case_when(
        difficulty_level == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
        difficulty_level == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
        difficulty_level == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
        TRUE ~ difficulty_level
      ),
      Effort = case_when(
        effort_condition == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
        effort_condition == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
        TRUE ~ effort_condition
      ),
      `Mean AUC` = "To be computed",
      `SD AUC` = "To be computed",
      `N Subjects` = "To be computed"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = gsub("\u2013", "-", Task_Group),
      Difficulty = gsub("\u2013", "-", Difficulty),
      Effort = gsub("\u2013", "-", Effort)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort) %>%
    select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, `Mean AUC`, `SD AUC`, `N Subjects`)
  
  tepr_placeholder %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
      locations = cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      row_group.as_column = FALSE,
      row_group.padding = px(8)
    ) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "TEPR data not available. Please ensure pupil data file contains cognitive_auc, task, effort_condition, and difficulty_level columns.",
      locations = cells_body()
    )
}

```{r}
#| label: pupil-evidence-setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false

# Extract pupil → drift coefficient from the pupil DDM model
pupil_drift_beta_str <- "[see tbl-pupil-ddm-fixef]"
pupil_drift_cri_str  <- ""
pupil_drift_null     <- "; credible interval includes zero"

pupil_bias_beta_str  <- "[see tbl-pupil-ddm-fixef]"
pupil_bias_cri_str   <- ""
pupil_bias_null      <- "; credible interval includes zero"

# Try to load the pupil fixed-effects table
pupil_fixef_obj <- NULL
for (obj_name in c("tblpupilcoef", "tblpupilfixef",
                   "pupilcoef", "pupil_fixef")) {
  if (exists(obj_name) && !is.null(get(obj_name))) {
    pupil_fixef_obj <- get(obj_name)
    break
  }
}

# If not already in environment, try loading from tables dir
if (is.null(pupil_fixef_obj)) {
  pupil_csv_candidates <- c(
    "pupilmodelfixef.csv",
    "pupilddmfixef.csv",
    "pupilfixedeffects.csv",
    "pupilcoefficients.csv"
  )
  for (csv_name in pupil_csv_candidates) {
    csv_path <- file.path(tables_dir, csv_name)
    if (file.exists(csv_path)) {
      pupil_fixef_obj <- readr::read_csv(csv_path,
                                         show_col_types = FALSE)
      break
    }
  }
}

# Extract pupil → drift row
if (!is.null(pupil_fixef_obj) && nrow(pupil_fixef_obj) > 0) {

  pdrift_row <- pupil_fixef_obj |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !grepl("^bs_|^bias_|^ndt_", term, ignore.case = TRUE),
      grepl("pupil|tepr|auc", term, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) |>
    dplyr::slice(1)

  if (nrow(pdrift_row) == 1) {
    pd_est <- pdrift_row$Estimate
    pd_lo  <- pdrift_row$Q2.5
    pd_hi  <- pdrift_row$Q97.5
    pupil_drift_beta_str <- sprintf("$\\beta = %.3f$", pd_est)
    pupil_drift_cri_str  <- sprintf("95%% CrI $[%.3f,\\; %.3f]$",
                                    pd_lo, pd_hi)
    pupil_drift_null     <- if (!is.na(pd_lo) && !is.na(pd_hi) &&
                                pd_lo < 0 && pd_hi > 0)
                              "; credible interval includes zero"
                            else ""
  }

  # Extract pupil → bias row
  pbias_row <- pupil_fixef_obj |>
    dplyr::filter(
      grepl("^bias_", term, ignore.case = TRUE),
      grepl("pupil|tepr|auc", term, ignore.case = TRUE)
    ) |>
    dplyr::slice(1)

  if (nrow(pbias_row) == 1) {
    pb_est <- pbias_row$Estimate
    pb_lo  <- pbias_row$Q2.5
    pb_hi  <- pbias_row$Q97.5
    pupil_bias_beta_str <- sprintf("$\\beta = %.3f$", pb_est)
    pupil_bias_cri_str  <- sprintf("95%% CrI $[%.3f,\\; %.3f]$",
                                   pb_lo, pb_hi)
    pupil_bias_null     <- if (!is.na(pb_lo) && !is.na(pb_hi) &&
                               pb_lo < 0 && pb_hi > 0)
                             "; credible interval includes zero"
                           else ""
  }
}
```

To explore whether any pupil-parameter association might be **conditional on task difficulty**, we fit a supplementary `pupil_scaled * difficulty` interaction model. If TEPR exerts qualitatively different influences across perceptual load conditions — as the Yerkes–Dodson framework would predict — the difficulty-conditional slopes should diverge, with arousal potentially boosting drift on Easy trials (where baseline drift is already positive) while remaining near zero or negative on Standard and Hard trials. However, this test is subject to the same TEPR measurement limitations noted above: because the AUC window may conflate motor-autonomic and cognitive signals, any difficulty-conditional pattern must be interpreted with caution. The difficulty-conditional posterior slopes of `pupil_scaled` on drift rate are visualized in @fig-pupil-drift-difficulty-interaction.

Pooled posterior coefficients for the trial-wise TEPR predictor were centered near zero for drift rate ($v$; `r pupil_drift_beta_str`, `r pupil_drift_cri_str`) and starting-point bias ($z$; `r pupil_bias_beta_str`, `r pupil_bias_cri_str`), with 95% CrIs spanning zero (@tbl-pupil-key-effects). Given the PSIS-LOO instability already noted, these coefficients — not ELPD rankings — are the defensible basis for pooled TEPR inference. The near-zero pattern suggests little incremental trial-wise information beyond behavioral predictors, but this conclusion remains **substantially weaker than the H2/H4 contrasts** because the TEPR window may conflate motor-autonomic and cognitive signals; the descriptive reversal under High effort (@tbl-tepr) is consistent with that concern. The data cannot distinguish a true absence of pupil-parameter coupling from a failed arousal index. Moment-matching LOO correction [@paananen2021] would be needed for reliable LOO estimates but was computationally prohibitive. Full fixed effects for pupil predictors are provided in Appendix~A6.

Pupil-augmented models were fit only to trials with valid pupil data (N $\approx$ `r format(n_trials_total, big.mark = ",")` trials). LOOIC values in @tbl-pupil-loo reflect predictive performance on this pupil-available subset and are not directly comparable to the full-sample behavioral models (@tbl-loo-comparison).

**Descriptive TEPR patterns and potential confounds.** An unexpected pattern emerged in the descriptive TEPR means (@tbl-tepr): in five of six experimental cells, mean TEPR magnitude was lower under High effort (40% MVC) than under Low effort (5% MVC). This reversal is counterintuitive if TEPR is interpreted as a direct index of cognitive arousal that should be elevated under High-effort conditions.

We consider two interpretations. First, the sustained isometric handgrip itself may generate competing autonomic signals — particularly increased sympathetic tone associated with muscular effort — that suppress or distort the task-evoked cognitive component of pupil dilation [@beatty1982; @loewenfeld1999]. Under this account, High effort trials contain a motor-driven pupil signal that interferes with the cognitive dilation component, reducing the observed TEPR even though cognitive demand remains high. Second, High effort may reduce task-focused cognitive processing by diverting limited attentional resources toward grip maintenance, thereby reducing the perceptual load indexed by TEPR — consistent with resource competition accounts of dual-task interference [@wickens2008].

Both interpretations converge on the conclusion that the Decision-Phase AUC (W3.0) TEPR window in this paradigm likely conflates motor/autonomic and cognitive components of pupil dilation, undermining its validity as a pure arousal index under the dual-task conditions examined here. This confound plausibly contributed to the null pupil-DDM coupling results reported above and underscores the interpretive limits of pupillometry in dual-task contexts involving sustained motor demands.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pupil-loo
#| tbl-cap: "Model comparison for pupil-augmented DDMs (within pupil-available trials only). The behavioral-only reference model (row 1) was fit on the same pupil-available trial subset to ensure direct comparability. Note. Pareto-$k$ diagnostics (max $k$ = 0.91) indicate PSIS-LOO estimates may be unreliable; model comparison should be interpreted cautiously and we rely primarily on posterior parameter estimates. ΔELPD values are relative to the behavioral-only reference."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"

pupil_loo_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "pupil_ddm", "tables", "pupil_loo_summary.csv")
if (!file.exists(pupil_loo_file)) {
  pupil_loo_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "ddm_pupil", "tables", "pupil_loo_summary.csv")
}

if (file.exists(pupil_loo_file)) {
  pupil_loo <- read_csv(pupil_loo_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  # DIAGNOSTIC: verify all models were fit on same trial subset
  if ("n_obs" %in% names(pupil_loo)) {
    n_obs_vals <- unique(pupil_loo$n_obs)
    if (length(n_obs_vals) > 1) {
      message(sprintf("[WARN] tbl-pupil-loo: models have DIFFERENT n_obs: %s -- LOO comparison invalid!", paste(n_obs_vals, collapse=", ")))
    } else {
      message(sprintf("[OK] tbl-pupil-loo: all models have n_obs = %s", n_obs_vals))
    }
  }
  # Map script names to reader-friendly labels; handle both model_name and model columns
  model_col <- if ("model_name" %in% names(pupil_loo)) "model_name" else "model"
  model_labels <- c(
    "model_0_behavioral" = "Behavioral only",
    "model_1_pupil_bias" = "Pupil on bias (z)",
    "model_2_pupil_bias_drift" = "Pupil on bias + drift (v, z)"
  )
  pupil_loo_display <- pupil_loo %>%
    mutate(
      Model = coalesce(model_labels[.data[[model_col]]], gsub("_", " ", .data[[model_col]])),
      across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))
    ) %>%
    select(-all_of(model_col)) %>%
    relocate(Model, .before = 1) %>%
    rename(
      `ELPD (LOO)` = elpd_loo,
      `SE(ELPD)` = se_elpd_loo,
      `LOOIC` = looic,
      `SE(LOOIC)` = looic_se,
      `Max Pareto k` = pareto_k_max,
      `ΔELPD` = delta_elpd,
      `ΔLOOIC` = delta_looic
    )
  pupil_loo_display %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"),
                 booktabs = TRUE,
                 linesep = "",
                 digits = 2) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"),
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::add_footnote(
      "Pareto-k max = 0.91; PSIS-LOO estimates may be unreliable. Interpret with caution.",
      notation = "none"
    )
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

```{r pupil-interaction-stats}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute caption choice and p_gt0 for fig-pupil-drift-difficulty-interaction and tbl-pupil-key-effects
pupil_fig_caption <- "Difficulty-Conditional TEPR Slopes on Drift Rate. Posterior distributions of the difficulty-conditional TEPR slope on drift rate $v$ for Standard, Hard, and Easy trials, from the pupil_scaled * difficulty interaction model. All three 95% credible intervals include zero, and the posteriors show minimal separation across difficulty levels, providing no clear evidence that trial-by-trial arousal fluctuations (indexed by TEPR) reliably predicted changes in evidence accumulation at any difficulty level. The absence of divergence across conditions is consistent with a null difficulty-conditional pattern, but interpretation is limited by the TEPR measurement confounds documented in the text (AUC window conflating motor-autonomic and cognitive components; see Section 3.6). Shaded regions show the 95% HDI; vertical dashed lines mark zero."
p_gt0_easy <- p_gt0_hard <- p_gt0_standard <- NA_real_
pupil_diff_mean_std <- pupil_diff_mean_hard <- pupil_diff_mean_easy <- NA_real_
pupil_diff_ci_std <- pupil_diff_ci_hard <- pupil_diff_ci_easy <- ""
pupil_includes_zero_std <- pupil_includes_zero_hard <- pupil_includes_zero_easy <- NA
pupil_slopes_note <- NULL
pupil_int_model_path <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "models",
                                  "pupil_interaction__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds")
if (file.exists(pupil_int_model_path) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit_pi <- tryCatch(readRDS(pupil_int_model_path), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(fit_pi) && inherits(fit_pi, "brmsfit")) {
    all_d <- brms::as_draws_df(fit_pi)
    all_names <- names(all_d)
    # Find the main pupil_scaled slope on drift (v/mu dpar, Standard = reference)
    # brms may prefix with "b_mu_" for the default dpar in Wiener models
    std_col <- intersect(c("b_pupil_scaled", "b_mu_pupil_scaled"), all_names)[1]
    # Find interaction columns: contains both "pupil_scaled" and difficulty level
    hard_col <- grep("pupil_scaled.*[Hh]ard|[Hh]ard.*pupil_scaled", all_names, value = TRUE)
    hard_col <- hard_col[!grepl("^b_bs_|^b_ndt_|^b_bias_|sd_|cor_|r_", hard_col)][1]
    easy_col <- grep("pupil_scaled.*[Ee]asy|[Ee]asy.*pupil_scaled", all_names, value = TRUE)
    easy_col <- easy_col[!grepl("^b_bs_|^b_ndt_|^b_bias_|sd_|cor_|r_", easy_col)][1]
    if (!is.na(std_col)) {
      draws_pupil_standard <- all_d[[std_col]]
      # Conditional slopes: main effect + interaction coefficient
      draws_pupil_hard <- if (!is.na(hard_col)) all_d[[std_col]] + all_d[[hard_col]] else all_d[[std_col]]
      draws_pupil_easy <- if (!is.na(easy_col)) all_d[[std_col]] + all_d[[easy_col]] else all_d[[std_col]]
      message(sprintf("[pupil-interaction-stats] std=%s | hard=%s | easy=%s",
                      std_col, if (is.na(hard_col)) "NOT FOUND" else hard_col,
                      if (is.na(easy_col)) "NOT FOUND" else easy_col))
      # ── Verification: raw interaction term means ──────────────────────────────
      if (!is.na(hard_col)) message(sprintf(
        "[pupil-interaction-stats] Raw interaction Hard term mean: %.4f", mean(all_d[[hard_col]])))
      if (!is.na(easy_col)) message(sprintf(
        "[pupil-interaction-stats] Raw interaction Easy term mean: %.4f", mean(all_d[[easy_col]])))
      p_gt0_easy     <- mean(draws_pupil_easy > 0)
      p_gt0_hard     <- mean(draws_pupil_hard > 0)
      p_gt0_standard <- mean(draws_pupil_standard > 0)
      pupil_diff_mean_std   <- mean(draws_pupil_standard)
      pupil_diff_mean_hard  <- mean(draws_pupil_hard)
      pupil_diff_mean_easy  <- mean(draws_pupil_easy)
      q_std <- quantile(draws_pupil_standard, c(0.025, 0.975))
      q_hard <- quantile(draws_pupil_hard, c(0.025, 0.975))
      q_easy <- quantile(draws_pupil_easy, c(0.025, 0.975))
      pupil_diff_ci_std    <- paste0("[", round(q_std[1], 3), ", ", round(q_std[2], 3), "]")
      pupil_diff_ci_hard   <- paste0("[", round(q_hard[1], 3), ", ", round(q_hard[2], 3), "]")
      pupil_diff_ci_easy   <- paste0("[", round(q_easy[1], 3), ", ", round(q_easy[2], 3), "]")
      pupil_includes_zero_std  <- q_std[1] <= 0 && q_std[2] >= 0
      pupil_includes_zero_hard <- q_hard[1] <= 0 && q_hard[2] >= 0
      pupil_includes_zero_easy <- q_easy[1] <= 0 && q_easy[2] >= 0
      med_easy  <- median(draws_pupil_easy)
      med_std   <- median(draws_pupil_standard)
      med_hard  <- median(draws_pupil_hard)
      hdi_easy  <- quantile(draws_pupil_easy, c(0.025, 0.975))
      use_option_a <- med_easy > 0 && (hdi_easy[2] > 0 || (hdi_easy[2] - hdi_easy[1]) * 0.5 > abs(hdi_easy[1])) &&
                      (abs(med_std) < 0.05 || med_std <= 0) && (abs(med_hard) < 0.05 || med_hard <= 0)
      if (use_option_a) {
        pupil_fig_caption <- "Difficulty-Conditional TEPR Slopes on Drift Rate. Posterior distributions of the difficulty-conditional TEPR slope on drift rate $v$, separately for Standard, Hard, and Easy trials, from the pupil_scaled * difficulty interaction model. The Easy condition shows a posterior slope with median above zero, and Standard and Hard conditions show slopes centered nearer to zero — a pattern qualitatively consistent with a Yerkes-Dodson difficulty-conditional account. However, all three 95% credible intervals include zero, so this divergence does not meet the threshold for a credible interaction effect. Additionally, all slopes are subject to the TEPR measurement limitations noted in the text (AUC window conflating motor-autonomic and cognitive components), which further limit causal interpretation. Shaded regions show the 95% HDI; vertical dashed lines mark zero."
      }
      # ── Near-identical slope detection ───────────────────────────────────────
      slopes_range <- max(c(pupil_diff_mean_std, pupil_diff_mean_hard, pupil_diff_mean_easy)) -
                      min(c(pupil_diff_mean_std, pupil_diff_mean_hard, pupil_diff_mean_easy))
      pupil_slopes_note <- if (!is.na(slopes_range) && slopes_range < 0.01) {
        paste0("*Note: Although the pupil\u00d7difficulty interaction was modeled, the three ",
               "difficulty-conditional slopes show minimal divergence (posterior means differ by ",
               sprintf("%.4f", slopes_range), " < 0.01), indicating that arousal effects on ",
               "drift rate do not vary meaningfully across task demands in this sample.*")
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    } else {
      message("[pupil-interaction-stats] Neither b_pupil_scaled nor b_mu_pupil_scaled found in draws.")
    }
  }
}
```

```{r null-evidence-pupil-apply}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# ── Apply null-evidence framework to pooled and conditional pupil effects ─────
# Requires: pd_est/pd_lo/pd_hi (pupil-evidence-setup),
#           pb_est/pb_lo/pb_hi (pupil-evidence-setup),
#           pupil_diff_mean_*/q_std/q_hard/q_easy/p_gt0_* (pupil-interaction-stats)
# All pupil effects are MEASUREMENT-LIMITED due to TEPR confound under sustained
# grip and unreliable PSIS-LOO (Pareto-k = 0.91).  They are therefore labelled
# "measurement-limited / inconclusive" regardless of posterior location.
# DO NOT interpret these as informative nulls.

# Helper: safely extract quantile pair from a numeric vector or named pair
safe_q <- function(q_vec, idx) {
  if (is.null(q_vec) || length(q_vec) < idx || is.na(q_vec[idx])) NA_real_
  else as.numeric(q_vec[idx])
}

# ── Pooled TEPR → drift (v) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
null_ev_pupil_drift <- safe_rope_summary(
  label           = "Pooled TEPR \u2192 Drift Rate (v)",
  parameter       = "v (identity link, pooled pupil model)",
  estimate        = if (exists("pd_est") && !is.null(pd_est)) pd_est else NA_real_,
  q2.5            = if (exists("pd_lo")  && !is.null(pd_lo))  pd_lo  else NA_real_,
  q97.5           = if (exists("pd_hi")  && !is.null(pd_hi))  pd_hi  else NA_real_,
  p_gt0           = NA_real_,
  rope_half_width = ROPE_V,
  design_limited  = FALSE,
  meas_limited    = TRUE,   # TEPR confounded by motor-autonomic signals; Pareto-k > 0.7
  scale_note      = "MEASUREMENT-LIMITED: TEPR likely confounds motor-autonomic and cognitive signals under sustained grip; PSIS-LOO unreliable (max Pareto-k = 0.91)."
)

# ── Pooled TEPR → bias (z) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
null_ev_pupil_bias <- safe_rope_summary(
  label           = "Pooled TEPR \u2192 Starting-Point Bias (z)",
  parameter       = "z (logit link, pooled pupil model)",
  estimate        = if (exists("pb_est") && !is.null(pb_est)) pb_est else NA_real_,
  q2.5            = if (exists("pb_lo")  && !is.null(pb_lo))  pb_lo  else NA_real_,
  q97.5           = if (exists("pb_hi")  && !is.null(pb_hi))  pb_hi  else NA_real_,
  p_gt0           = NA_real_,
  rope_half_width = ROPE_BIAS,
  design_limited  = FALSE,
  meas_limited    = TRUE,
  scale_note      = "MEASUREMENT-LIMITED: same TEPR confound as pooled drift model."
)

# ── Difficulty-conditional TEPR slopes on drift ──────────────────────────────
# CrI comes from quantile vectors q_std, q_hard, q_easy (pupil-interaction-stats).
# These exist only when the interaction model loaded; safe_q() handles absence.

null_ev_pupil_std <- safe_rope_summary(
  label           = "TEPR slope on drift \u2014 Standard trials",
  parameter       = "v (identity link, interaction model)",
  estimate        = if (exists("pupil_diff_mean_std")  && !is.na(pupil_diff_mean_std))
                      pupil_diff_mean_std  else NA_real_,
  q2.5            = safe_q(if (exists("q_std"))  q_std  else NULL, 1),
  q97.5           = safe_q(if (exists("q_std"))  q_std  else NULL, 2),
  p_gt0           = if (exists("p_gt0_standard") && !is.na(p_gt0_standard))
                      p_gt0_standard else NA_real_,
  rope_half_width = ROPE_V,
  design_limited  = FALSE,
  meas_limited    = TRUE,
  scale_note      = "MEASUREMENT-LIMITED: conditional slope from pupil_scaled * difficulty interaction; TEPR confound applies to all difficulty levels."
)

null_ev_pupil_hard <- safe_rope_summary(
  label           = "TEPR slope on drift \u2014 Hard trials",
  parameter       = "v (identity link, interaction model)",
  estimate        = if (exists("pupil_diff_mean_hard") && !is.na(pupil_diff_mean_hard))
                      pupil_diff_mean_hard else NA_real_,
  q2.5            = safe_q(if (exists("q_hard"))  q_hard  else NULL, 1),
  q97.5           = safe_q(if (exists("q_hard"))  q_hard  else NULL, 2),
  p_gt0           = if (exists("p_gt0_hard") && !is.na(p_gt0_hard))
                      p_gt0_hard else NA_real_,
  rope_half_width = ROPE_V,
  design_limited  = FALSE,
  meas_limited    = TRUE,
  scale_note      = "MEASUREMENT-LIMITED: conditional slope from pupil_scaled * difficulty interaction; TEPR confound applies."
)

null_ev_pupil_easy <- safe_rope_summary(
  label           = "TEPR slope on drift \u2014 Easy trials",
  parameter       = "v (identity link, interaction model)",
  estimate        = if (exists("pupil_diff_mean_easy") && !is.na(pupil_diff_mean_easy))
                      pupil_diff_mean_easy else NA_real_,
  q2.5            = safe_q(if (exists("q_easy"))  q_easy  else NULL, 1),
  q97.5           = safe_q(if (exists("q_easy"))  q_easy  else NULL, 2),
  p_gt0           = if (exists("p_gt0_easy") && !is.na(p_gt0_easy))
                      p_gt0_easy else NA_real_,
  rope_half_width = ROPE_V,
  design_limited  = FALSE,
  meas_limited    = TRUE,
  scale_note      = "MEASUREMENT-LIMITED: conditional slope from pupil_scaled * difficulty interaction; TEPR confound applies."
)

# ── Combine all rows into the master null-evidence summary ──────────────────
null_evidence_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  null_evidence_h_partial,   # H2, H3, H4 (defined in null-evidence-helpers)
  null_ev_pupil_drift,
  null_ev_pupil_bias,
  null_ev_pupil_std,
  null_ev_pupil_hard,
  null_ev_pupil_easy
)

# ── Appendix-ready detailed table ───────────────────────────────────────────
null_evidence_appendix <- null_evidence_summary %>%
  dplyr::select(label, parameter, estimate, q2.5, q97.5,
                cri_width, ci_includes_zero, p_gt0, p_in_rope,
                rope_half_width, design_limited, meas_limited,
                evidence_label, scale_note)

# ── Main display table (formatted) ──────────────────────────────────────────
null_evidence_display <- format_posterior_summary(null_evidence_summary)

# ── Machine-readable inline summary ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Used to generate safer inline text in Discussion if needed.
ne_label <- function(target_label) {
  null_evidence_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(target_label, label, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(evidence_label) %>%
    dplyr::first() %||% "classification unavailable"
}
ne_rope_pct <- function(target_label) {
  v <- null_evidence_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(target_label, label, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(p_in_rope) %>%
    dplyr::first()
  if (is.null(v) || is.na(v)) "–" else sprintf("%.0f%%", v * 100)
}
ne_cri <- function(target_label) {
  row <- null_evidence_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(target_label, label, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
    dplyr::slice(1)
  if (nrow(row) == 0 || is.na(row$q2.5) || is.na(row$q97.5)) return("–")
  sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", row$q2.5, row$q97.5)
}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pupil-key-effects
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Key pupil effects on drift ($v$) and bias ($z$) (link scale). Posterior mean, 95% CrI, whether the interval includes zero, and $P(\\\\beta > 0)$ for difficulty-conditional slopes (from interaction model).", if (!is.null(pupil_slopes_note)) paste0(" ", pupil_slopes_note) else "")
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"

pupil_key_terms_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "pupil_ddm", "tables", "pupil_effects_key_terms.csv")
if (!file.exists(pupil_key_terms_file)) {
  pupil_key_terms_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "ddm_pupil", "tables", "pupil_effects_key_terms.csv")
}

if (file.exists(pupil_key_terms_file)) {
  pupil_key_terms <- read_csv(pupil_key_terms_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  cn <- names(pupil_key_terms)
  est_col <- intersect(c("Estimate", "estimate", "mean"), cn)[1]
  q2_col <- intersect(c("Q2.5", "q2.5", "q_2.5"), cn)[1]
  q97_col <- intersect(c("Q97.5", "q97.5", "q_97.5"), cn)[1]
  term_col <- intersect(c("term", "parameter", "Parameter"), cn)[1]
  if (is.na(est_col)) est_col <- cn[1]
  if (is.na(term_col)) term_col <- cn[1]
  if (!is.na(q2_col) && !is.na(q97_col) && q2_col %in% cn && q97_col %in% cn) {
    pupil_key_terms_display <- pupil_key_terms %>%
      mutate(
        mean = round(.data[[est_col]], 3),
        `95% CrI` = paste0("[", round(.data[[q2_col]], 3), ", ", round(.data[[q97_col]], 3), "]"),
        `Includes 0` = ifelse(.data[[q2_col]] <= 0 & .data[[q97_col]] >= 0, "Yes", "No"),
        p_gt0 = NA_real_,
        term_display = case_when(
          "dpar" %in% cn & .data[["dpar"]] == "v" ~ "Pupil $v$",
          "dpar" %in% cn & .data[["dpar"]] == "bias" ~ "Pupil $z$",
          grepl("drift", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) & !grepl("bias", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pupil $v$",
          grepl("bias", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pupil $z$",
          TRUE ~ as.character(.data[[term_col]])
        )
      ) %>%
      # Keep one row per parameter type (deduplicate): first row per v/z
      group_by(term_display) %>%
      slice(1) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      arrange(factor(term_display, levels = c("Pupil $v$", "Pupil $z$"))) %>%
      select(term_display, mean, `95% CrI`, `Includes 0`, p_gt0) %>%
      rename(Parameter = term_display)
    # Append difficulty-conditional rows from interaction model when available
    if (!is.na(p_gt0_easy) && !is.na(p_gt0_hard) && !is.na(p_gt0_standard)) {
      diff_rows <- tibble::tibble(
        Parameter = c("Pupil $v$: Standard", "Pupil $v$: Hard", "Pupil $v$: Easy"),
        mean = c(round(pupil_diff_mean_std, 3), round(pupil_diff_mean_hard, 3), round(pupil_diff_mean_easy, 3)),
        `95% CrI` = c(pupil_diff_ci_std, pupil_diff_ci_hard, pupil_diff_ci_easy),
        `Includes 0` = c(
          if (isTRUE(pupil_includes_zero_std)) "Yes" else "No",
          if (isTRUE(pupil_includes_zero_hard)) "Yes" else "No",
          if (isTRUE(pupil_includes_zero_easy)) "Yes" else "No"
        ),
        p_gt0 = c(p_gt0_standard, p_gt0_hard, p_gt0_easy)
      )
      pupil_key_terms_display <- dplyr::bind_rows(pupil_key_terms_display, diff_rows)
    }
    pupil_key_terms_display <- pupil_key_terms_display %>%
      mutate(`P(β > 0)` = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(p_gt0) ~ NA_character_,
        round(p_gt0, 3) >= 0.999 ~ "> .999",
        round(p_gt0, 3) <= 0.001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p_gt0)
      )) %>%
      select(Parameter, mean, `95% CrI`, `Includes 0`, `P(β > 0)`)
  } else {
    pupil_key_terms_display <- pupil_key_terms %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
  }
  kbl_args <- list(
    format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"),
                 booktabs = TRUE,
                 linesep = "",
    digits = 3
  )
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    kbl_args$escape <- FALSE
    if (ncol(pupil_key_terms_display) == 5) {
      kbl_args$col.names <- c("Parameter", "Mean", "95\\% CrI", "Includes 0", "$P(\\beta > 0)$")
    }
  }
  do.call(knitr::kable, c(list(pupil_key_terms_display), kbl_args)) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}

```{r}
#| label: fig-pupil-drift-difficulty-interaction
#| fig-cap: !expr pupil_fig_caption
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "90%"

# Load the pupil interaction model
pupil_int_model_path <- file.path(
  proj_root, params$run_dir, "models",
  "pupil_interaction__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds"
)

if (file.exists(pupil_int_model_path) &&
    requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {

  fit_pupil_int <- tryCatch(readRDS(pupil_int_model_path), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(fit_pupil_int) && inherits(fit_pupil_int, "brmsfit")) {
    draws_int <- tryCatch({
      all_draws <- brms::as_draws_df(fit_pupil_int)
      nn <- names(all_draws)
      # Find main slope (Standard reference): brms may prefix with b_mu_ for Wiener family
      std_c <- intersect(c("b_pupil_scaled", "b_mu_pupil_scaled"), nn)[1]
      if (is.na(std_c)) stop("No pupil_scaled main-effect column found in draws")
      # Find interaction columns: must contain pupil_scaled AND the difficulty level
      # Exclude bs/ndt/bias dpars and random-effect draws
      hard_c <- grep("pupil_scaled.*[Hh]ard|[Hh]ard.*pupil_scaled", nn, value = TRUE)
      hard_c <- hard_c[!grepl("^b_bs_|^b_ndt_|^b_bias_|sd_|cor_|r_", hard_c)][1]
      easy_c <- grep("pupil_scaled.*[Ee]asy|[Ee]asy.*pupil_scaled", nn, value = TRUE)
      easy_c <- easy_c[!grepl("^b_bs_|^b_ndt_|^b_bias_|sd_|cor_|r_", easy_c)][1]
      message(sprintf("[fig-pupil-drift] std=%s | hard=%s | easy=%s",
                      std_c,
                      if (is.na(hard_c)) "NOT FOUND" else hard_c,
                      if (is.na(easy_c)) "NOT FOUND" else easy_c))
      if (!is.na(hard_c)) message(sprintf(
        "[fig-pupil-drift] Raw interaction Hard term mean: %.4f", mean(all_draws[[hard_c]])))
      if (!is.na(easy_c)) message(sprintf(
        "[fig-pupil-drift] Raw interaction Easy term mean: %.4f", mean(all_draws[[easy_c]])))
      # Build difficulty-conditional slopes: Standard = main; Hard/Easy = main + interaction
      std_draws  <- all_draws[[std_c]]
      hard_draws <- if (!is.na(hard_c)) std_draws + all_draws[[hard_c]] else std_draws
      easy_draws <- if (!is.na(easy_c)) std_draws + all_draws[[easy_c]] else std_draws
      message(sprintf("[fig-pupil-drift] Conditional slope means: Std=%.4f Hard=%.4f Easy=%.4f",
                      mean(std_draws), mean(hard_draws), mean(easy_draws)))
      tibble::tibble(
        difficulty = factor(
          rep(c("Standard", "Hard", "Easy"), each = length(std_draws)),
          levels = c("Standard", "Hard", "Easy")
        ),
        slope = c(std_draws, hard_draws, easy_draws)
      )
    }, error = function(e) { message("draws extraction failed: ", e$message); NULL })

    if (!is.null(draws_int) && nrow(draws_int) > 0) {
      # Compute 95% quantile intervals per difficulty level
      hdi_int <- draws_int %>%
        dplyr::group_by(difficulty) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(
          lo  = quantile(slope, 0.025),
          hi  = quantile(slope, 0.975),
          med = median(slope),
          .groups = "drop"
        )

      fill_colors <- c("Standard" = "#4393C3", "Hard" = "#D6604D", "Easy" = "#4DAC26")

      p_pupil_interact <- ggplot(draws_int, aes(x = slope)) +
        geom_density(aes(fill = difficulty), alpha = 0.75, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
        geom_segment(
          data = hdi_int,
          aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = -Inf, yend = -Inf),
          color = "black", linewidth = 1.2
        ) +
        geom_point(
          data = hdi_int,
          aes(x = med, y = 0),
          shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 1.5
        ) +
        facet_wrap(~ difficulty, nrow = 1) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors, guide = "none") +
        labs(
          x = "Posterior slope: pupil_scaled on drift rate (v)",
          y = "Posterior density"
        ) +
        theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
        theme(
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
          strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
        )
      print(p_pupil_interact)
    } else {
      message("Pupil interaction draws could not be extracted.")
      invisible(NULL)
    }
  } else {
    message("Pupil interaction model not available (NULL or non-brmsfit).")
    invisible(NULL)
  }
} else {
  message("Pupil interaction model file or brms package not found; skipping figure.")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

Importantly, Figure 10 provides the direct statistical test of whether arousal effects on evidence accumulation are heterogeneous across task difficulty. Each panel shows the full posterior distribution of the pupil–drift coupling coefficient for that difficulty stratum — the slope of pupil_scaled predicting $v$. Posterior probability $P(\beta_\text{pupil} > 0)$ for each difficulty level is reported in @tbl-pupil-key-effects.

model_path_diff <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "models",
                              "additive__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds")

if (file.exists(model_path_diff) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tryCatch({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(brms); library(posterior) })
    fit_diff <- readRDS(model_path_diff)
    d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit_diff)

    # Drift contrasts: Hard vs Standard = b_difficulty_3Hard
    #                  Easy vs Standard = b_difficulty_3Easy
    #                  Easy vs Hard     = b_difficulty_3Easy - b_difficulty_3Hard
    has_v_hard <- "b_difficulty_3Hard" %in% names(d)
    has_v_easy <- "b_difficulty_3Easy" %in% names(d)
    # Boundary contrasts: bs_ prefix
    has_a_hard <- "b_bs_difficulty_3Hard" %in% names(d)
    has_a_easy <- "b_bs_difficulty_3Easy" %in% names(d)

    make_contrast_df <- function(draws_vec, label) {
      tibble::tibble(diff = draws_vec, contrast = label)
    }

    v_contrasts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      if (has_v_hard) make_contrast_df(d[["b_difficulty_3Hard"]], "Hard - Standard (v)"),
      if (has_v_easy) make_contrast_df(d[["b_difficulty_3Easy"]], "Easy - Standard (v)"),
      if (has_v_hard && has_v_easy)
        make_contrast_df(d[["b_difficulty_3Easy"]] - d[["b_difficulty_3Hard"]], "Easy - Hard (v)")
    )
    a_contrasts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      if (has_a_hard) make_contrast_df(d[["b_bs_difficulty_3Hard"]], "Hard - Standard (a)"),
      if (has_a_easy) make_contrast_df(d[["b_bs_difficulty_3Easy"]], "Easy - Standard (a)"),
      if (has_a_hard && has_a_easy)
        make_contrast_df(d[["b_bs_difficulty_3Easy"]] - d[["b_bs_difficulty_3Hard"]], "Easy - Hard (a)")
    )

    plot_posterior_contrasts <- function(df, title, fill_col) {
      hdi_tbl <- df %>%
        dplyr::group_by(contrast) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(lo = quantile(diff, 0.025), hi = quantile(diff, 0.975),
                         med = median(diff), .groups = "drop")
      ggplot(df, aes(x = diff, fill = contrast)) +
        geom_density(alpha = 0.75, color = "black", linewidth = 0.35) +
        geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
        geom_segment(data = hdi_tbl,
                     aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = -Inf, yend = -Inf),
                     color = "black", linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        geom_point(data = hdi_tbl, aes(x = med, y = 0),
                   shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "black", size = 1.3,
                   inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        facet_wrap(~ contrast, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
        scale_fill_brewer(palette = fill_col, guide = "none") +
        labs(x = "Posterior difference (link scale)", y = "Density", title = title) +
        theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
        theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
              strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92"),
              panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
    }

    if (nrow(v_contrasts) > 0 && nrow(a_contrasts) > 0) {
      library(patchwork)
      p_v <- plot_posterior_contrasts(v_contrasts, "Drift rate (v) contrasts", "Blues")
      p_a <- plot_posterior_contrasts(a_contrasts, "Boundary separation (a) contrasts", "Reds")
      print(p_v / p_a)
    } else {
      message("Not enough contrast draws available.")
      invisible(NULL)
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Difficulty posterior contrasts failed: ", e$message)
    invisible(NULL)
  })
} else {
  message("Model or required packages not found; skipping difficulty contrast plot.")
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

Pairwise difficulty contrasts for drift rate ($v$) and boundary separation ($a$) — with all three 95% CrIs excluding zero — are presented in @fig-difficulty-contrasts (Section 3.4).

**Boundary separation ($a$)**: Easy trials have narrower decision boundaries, consistent with reduced caution when discrimination is easier.

The primary findings were robust to alternative RT cutoff thresholds (0.15 s and 0.25 s); full sensitivity parameter estimates are reported in Appendix A4.2.

# Discussion

## Summary of Key Findings

Results confirmed Hypothesis 1 (H1): High effort reduced drift rate, consistent with resource competition or supra-optimal arousal (Section 3.4.1). For Hypothesis 2 (H2), the posterior for the boundary-separation effort contrast was concentrated near zero and the 95% CrI spanned zero, providing no credible evidence of boundary widening — a finding inconsistent with the AGT-derived prediction of compensatory caution adjustment [@astonjones2005], though the near-zero estimate is not a formal disconfirmation in the absence of a pre-specified equivalence threshold (Section 3.4.1). Hypothesis 3 (H3) could not be tested directly: the response-signal design required constraining $t_0$ to an intercept-only specification for model stability, so no primary-model test of H3 was possible; an exploratory effort coefficient on $\log t_0$ was small and highly imprecise, and no firm conclusion about peripheral slowing can be drawn from it (Section 3.4.1). For Hypothesis 4 (H4), starting-point bias showed a near-zero, uncertain effort contrast, providing no credible evidence of a shift toward neutrality under High effort — again a graded rather than a definitive null (Section 3.5). Importantly, while High effort reduced **accuracy** (manipulation check: $\beta = -0.16$, $p < .001$), it did not reliably slow **reaction time** ($\beta = 0.02$ s, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.05]). This dissociation — lower accuracy without RT slowing — is explained by the DDM decomposition: drift rate declined (evidence quality), while the boundary-separation contrast remained near zero (no detected compensatory caution increase), consistent with the DDM prediction of faster errors rather than slower correct responses under degraded drift. The effort → drift effect was robust to task (ADT vs. VDT) inclusion (Appendix~A4.3). Trial-wise pupil-linked arousal (TEPR) showed near-zero posterior associations with both drift rate and starting-point bias (Section 3.6); however, these inferences are weaker than the H2/H4 behavioral nulls because PSIS-LOO model comparison was unreliable (max Pareto-$k = 0.91$) and the TEPR window likely conflates cognitive and motor-autonomic components under sustained grip conditions. The overall pattern is most consistent with the "detrimental impact" hypothesis grounded in Resource Competition theory [@azer2023; @wickens2008], which predicts that concurrent physical effort degrades the quality of evidence accumulation. The absence of comparably strong evidence for a boundary-separation increase is, at minimum, inconsistent with a strong form of the "adaptive caution" hypothesis (Strategic Adaptation) — though that inference remains graded rather than definitive.

## The "Crunch Point": Why Drift Rate Declined

The reduction in drift rate under High effort (40% MVC) relative to Low effort is the central finding of this study and directly supports H1. Interpreted through Adaptive Gain Theory [@astonjones2005], this result is consistent with an inverted-U arousal–performance relationship: the 40% MVC handgrip exerted sufficient physiological demand to push older adults into the supra-optimal arousal zone, where noise in neural representations degrades the signal-to-noise ratio driving evidence accumulation [@mather2016; @mikneviciute2022]. Critically, the DDM framework localizes this performance decrement to *evidence quality* ($v$): boundary separation ($a$) yielded a near-zero effort contrast with no credible evidence of compensatory widening, and non-decision time ($t_0$) could not be directly tested given the response-signal design constraint (see Section 3.4.1 and the H3 discussion below). The implication is theoretically important: among parameters identified with adequate precision here, the cost of effort-induced arousal in older adults is most plausibly borne by a degradation in the rate at which task-relevant information is integrated, rather than by strategic slowing or conservative criterion shifts on $a$ or $z$. Peripheral encoding and motor components within $t_0$ were not separately identified in the primary specification, so that channel remains unresolved rather than ruled out. Prior work on effort-related performance decline in older adults [@azer2023; @wickens2008] could not isolate this mechanism; the DDM decomposition provides that mechanistic specificity where the evidence is available.

```{r}

This visualizes why older adults' reaction times become disproportionately variable and slow when physical effort or task difficulty degrades the quality of evidence accumulation ($v$)."
