## Modeling Constraints: Non-Decision Time and Peripheral Processes

The inability to directly test H3 reflects a structural constraint of the response-signal paradigm: because the response window is externally gated, $t_0$ cannot be cleanly disentangled from the timing structure, necessitating an intercept-only specification for model stability (@sec-ddm-spec). H3 is therefore not testable within the primary analysis. Exploratory models that permitted $t_0$ to vary by effort yielded a small but highly imprecise **coefficient on $\log t_0$** ($\hat{\beta} = 0.02$, 95% CrI $[-0.05,\; 0.09]$ on that scale). Because the interval spans zero and the effect is parameterized on the log link, no reliable millisecond-scale summary follows without committing to a baseline $t_0$; the CrI is compatible with both negligible and large multiplicative changes in non-decision time, precluding firm conclusions about peripheral slowing. This estimate is consistent with the view that isometric grip tasks at moderate intensities primarily engage central rather than peripheral resources [@wickens2008], but it does not constitute a reliable test of that proposition. The accuracy decline under High effort (@tbl-accuracy-glmm) aligns most directly with reductions in drift rate ($v$) rather than with shifts in $t_0$ — consistent with, but not confirming, an interpretation that cognitive-motor interference operated primarily during evidence accumulation.

## Strategic Rigidity: Why Caution ($a$) Didn't Increase

The H2 posterior is near-zero and potentially, though not definitively, theoretically informative. The effort contrast on $a$ was concentrated near zero with the 95% CrI spanning zero (`r h2_beta_str`, `r h2_cri_str``r h2_null_note`), consistent with at most a small caution adjustment — but because no pre-specified equivalence threshold was used, the appropriate reading is "no credible evidence of a compensatory increase" rather than strong disconfirmation. In natural-scale terms, the posterior median corresponds to `r h2_natural_pct_str` of baseline boundary separation ($\hat{a} \approx$ `r a_standard` in the Standard condition; @tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort) — smaller than the routine variation in $a$ across difficulty levels ($\hat{a}$ ranging from `r a_hard` to `r a_standard`). Adaptive Gain Theory [@astonjones2005] predicts that phasic locus coeruleus–norepinephrine (LC-NE) activation promotes a shift toward *exploitation* of current task strategy, manifest as widening of the decision criterion. Empirical support for this prediction comes from @cavanagh2014, who showed that pupil-indexed arousal during high-conflict choices predicted increased boundary separation — though that manipulation targeted transient cognitive conflict rather than sustained physical effort. Why the prediction may not extend to sustained grip is open: one possibility is that aging compresses or blunts the phasic LC-NE response under high metabolic load [@mather2016; @huang2024]; another is that the sustained nature of the grip manipulation simply does not engage the phasic LC-NE gain mechanism that drives criterion widening in conflict paradigms. Resolving these accounts requires direct measurement of LC integrity and phasic NE dynamics — precisely the aim of the broader LC-BAP project of which this chapter is a part.

Notably, boundary estimates did vary by stimulus-driven difficulty (Easy: `r a_easy`, Standard: `r a_standard`, Hard: `r a_hard`; @tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort), confirming that the model is sensitive to caution adjustments driven by bottom-up perceptual demands, even though no credible effort-related adjustment was detected. Future work using free-response paradigms (without response cues) could better isolate strategic flexibility from design-imposed temporal constraints and provide a more powerful test of whether effort at 40% MVC influences decision caution.

A potential concern with response-side coding is whether the Wiener DDM misinterprets Standard trial responses — where the correct answer is 'Same' (lower boundary) — as errors, because they accumulate toward a negative drift (lower boundary rather than upper). This concern does not apply in the present implementation. The decresponse argument in brms encodes the observed response (Different = 1, Same = 0) as the boundary indicator, not a correctness flag. The model observes the actual RT and response, infers the latent evidence trajectory that would produce that RT–accuracy combination given the full design, and estimates parameters that best explain the joint RT × accuracy distribution across all conditions simultaneously. Accordingly, the strong negative drift on Standard trials ($\hat{v} \approx -1.09$) does not indicate that the model treats these as error trials; it correctly captures the fact that participants accurately pressed 'Same' by accumulating evidence toward the lower boundary. The fact that boundary separation is higher on Standard trials ($\hat{a} = 2.64$) than on Hard ($\hat{a} = 2.37$) or Easy ($\hat{a} = 2.41$) further validates this interpretation: the model responds to the exhaustive search demands of Standard trials by estimating a wider, more cautious boundary — the theoretically correct direction — rather than collapsing the boundary as it would if it incorrectly coded these as high-error conditions.

**Boundary separation vs. starting-point bias: Different timescales of adjustment.** It is important to clarify an apparent asymmetry in the modeling decisions. Starting-point bias $z$ was constrained to be constant across difficulty levels, reflecting the logical impossibility of pre-trial criterion adjustment when trial difficulty is randomized and unknown prior to stimulus onset. In contrast, boundary separation $a$ was estimated as a function of difficulty and varied systematically (Standard: $\hat{a}$ = `r a_standard`; Hard: $\hat{a}$ = `r a_hard`; Easy: $\hat{a}$ = `r a_easy`; @tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort).

This is not a contradiction. The two parameters reflect adjustments occurring at different timescales. Starting-point bias $z$ represents a true pre-stimulus strategic choice — where participants position themselves before evidence accumulation begins — and can only be set based on information available before the trial (task modality, effort condition). Boundary separation $a$, by contrast, is not a pre-trial strategic decision but rather an effective decision threshold inferred by the model from the shape of the empirical RT distribution within each condition. Participants do not "set" this boundary in advance; rather, the model recovers it as the latent parameter that best explains the observed RT variance under diffusion process assumptions [@ratcliff1985; @voss2004interpreting]. Over many trials, difficulty-dependent differences in RT dispersion and accuracy produce systematically different $a$ estimates even though individual participants are unaware of upcoming difficulty.

The larger $a$ on Standard trials reflects the model's accommodation of the characteristically broader, more right-skewed RT distribution observed on those trials — a distributional signature of the exhaustive comparison process required to confirm perfect sameness [@farell1985; @voss2004interpreting]. In this sense, $a$ captures the mechanistic consequence of within-trial processing demands, while $z$ captures a pre-trial strategic bias. Both are legitimate sources of condition-specific variation, but only $z$ requires advance knowledge of the trial type.

```{r bias-inline-compute}
#| echo: false
#| include: false
# Compute overall bias mean and CrI for inline use
z_overall_mean <- 0.63
z_overall_q2.5 <- 0.58
z_overall_q97.5 <- 0.68
if (!is.null(std_bias_levels) && nrow(std_bias_levels) > 0) {
  bias_overall <- std_bias_levels %>%
    filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT)
  if (nrow(bias_overall) > 0 && "z_mean" %in% names(bias_overall)) {
    z_overall_mean <- round(mean(bias_overall$z_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    z_overall_q2.5 <- round(mean(bias_overall$z_q2.5, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
    z_overall_q97.5 <- round(mean(bias_overall$z_q97.5, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  }
}
```

## Bias and Phasic Arousal

The near-zero effort contrast on starting-point bias (H4; `r h4_beta_str`, `r h4_cri_str``r h4_p0_str`) provides no credible evidence that concurrent handgrip at 40% MVC shifted pre-existing response preferences in older adults — though the credible interval does not formally exclude a small effect, and no equivalence threshold was established. A key interpretive consideration is the distinction between tonic and phasic arousal: the @degee2020pupil bias-resetting effect was demonstrated using phasic, within-trial arousal fluctuations indexed by pupil dilation, whereas the present H4 test relied on a sustained tonic effort manipulation. Tonic arousal elevation may not produce the same criterion-resetting dynamics as a phasic arousal event — a distinction that future work pairing trial-level TEPR with starting-point bias estimates could address directly. Starting-point bias was consistently above 0.5 across all conditions ($z = `r z_overall_mean`$, 95% CrI [`r z_overall_q2.5`, `r z_overall_q97.5`]; @tbl-standard-only-bias-levels), reflecting a stable liberal tendency toward "different" responses that the effort contrast does not credibly shift.

Critically, this pattern reflects a **liberal** response bias in Signal Detection Theory terms — participants were predisposed to report "Different" with relatively low evidentiary thresholds. This contrasts with the conservative recognition criterion (high $\beta$, reflected in a response bias *away* from "old" or "signal") typically reported in older adults in episodic recognition memory tasks [@koen2016]. The present paradigm is a change-detection task, not a recognition memory task, and the "Different" response corresponds to detecting a *signal* (a change is present). A starting point biased toward "Different" therefore reflects a liberal detection strategy — more false alarms, fewer misses — not a conservative one.

The liberal detection strategy is consistent with the "Different-as-default heuristic" documented in same-different paradigms [@farell1985; @nosofsky1997palmeri]: detecting any mismatch is self-terminating (the comparison can stop at the first discrepant feature), whereas confirming sameness requires exhaustive feature comparison. Under concurrent grip load at 40% MVC, adopting a liberal "Different" starting point reduces the cognitive expense of Standard (Same) trials at the cost of reduced discrimination accuracy — a sensible tradeoff when both arousal and response-time pressure are elevated. The absence of a credible effort contrast on starting-point bias is consistent with this being a deeply habituated task strategy rather than a state-dependent adjustment to momentary arousal, though this interpretation is not uniquely supported given the graded nature of the null.

The absence of a detectable phasic bias-resetting effect stands in contrast to prior work showing that pupil-indexed arousal can shift response criterion in younger adults [@degee2020pupil], and may reflect age-related attenuation of phasic LC-NE signals [@huang2024]. The pupil-linked findings in this chapter, however, must be classified as inconclusive rather than informative nulls. As detailed in Section 3.6, three overlapping limitations constrain interpretation: (1) posterior coefficients for TEPR on both drift rate and bias were near zero; (2) PSIS-LOO model comparison was unreliable (max Pareto-$k = 0.91$), precluding valid ELPD-based model selection; and (3) the unexpected reversal of TEPR magnitude under High relative to Low effort (@tbl-tepr) suggests that the Decision-Phase AUC window conflates motor-autonomic with cognitive dilation under sustained grip. These limitations collectively mean the current data cannot distinguish a genuine absence of pupil-parameter coupling from a failure of the TEPR measure to isolate cognitive arousal. Future work using a non-motor effort manipulation or a temporally sharper pupil window would be needed to resolve this. The task-level bias difference, by contrast, is robust to all of these concerns: older adults showed a reliably stronger tendency toward *different* responses in the ADT than the VDT ($\Delta z = -0.04$, 95% CrI [−0.06, −0.02]; @tbl-standard-only-bias-contrasts), a contrast excluding zero that likely reflects the perceptual asymmetry of the auditory paradigm, where frequency offsets produce a more salient "different" signal than the luminance changes of the VDT. Whether LC integrity moderates this task-specific liberal bias — given the LC's role in sensory gating [@mather2016; @huang2024] — is a question for future work.

## Limitations and Future Directions

Several limitations constrain the interpretation of these findings. First, the standard Wiener DDM assumes constant drift within each trial and does not include across-trial variability in drift ($s_v$), starting point ($s_z$), or non-decision time ($s_{t_0}$). This produced localized fast-tail misfit, most pronounced in Easy VDT conditions, where the model underpredicted the frequency of very fast correct responses — likely reflecting a subset of anticipatory responses or an extremely high-drift regime incompatible with the Wiener process at the cell level. Sensitivity analyses using 2% fast-response censoring and visual inspection of mid-body quantile-probability plots confirmed that this misfit did not alter the direction or credibility of any key parameter contrast (Appendix A3). Future extensions incorporating across-trial variability, a fast-guess contaminant mixture, or urgency-collapsing boundaries may improve absolute fit, particularly for Easy trials [@ratcliff2008diffusion].

Second, the response-signal paradigm imposes structural constraints on parameter estimation. Because the response window is externally gated, non-decision time $t_0$ could not be estimated with condition-specific variation without instability (@sec-ddm-spec and the H3 discussion above), limiting the direct test of H3. Reaction times are measured from response-screen onset rather than stimulus onset, confining the interpretation of $t_0$ to motor execution and response selection rather than early perceptual encoding. These design choices were necessary given the MRI-compatible grip-force paradigm but limit generalizability to free-response paradigms where $t_0$ reflects the full encoding-decision-motor chain.

Third, the trial-wise pupil predictor (Decision-Phase AUC; W3.0) spans both pre- and post-response epochs, making it difficult to isolate phasic arousal during evidence accumulation from post-decisional pupil dynamics. Although RT was included as a covariate in all pupil-DDM models to partial out response-timing confounds, we did not test sensitivity to AUC window definition (e.g., a pre-response W1.3 window). Additionally, PSIS-LOO estimates for pupil-augmented models were unreliable (Pareto-$k > 0.7$), so model comparison was limited; conclusions about pupil effects are based on posterior coefficient distributions rather than LOO-based model selection [@vehtari2017loo].

Fourth, the concurrent isometric handgrip manipulation (40% MVC) may interact with motor execution in ways not fully captured by small fixed effects on $t_0$; future work integrating EMG or kinematic measures could disentangle central resource competition from peripheral motor interference. Linear Ballistic Accumulator or race models may also better accommodate the fast-tail RT dynamics observed in Easy-difficulty conditions, and future work could explore whether these model families yield the same substantive pattern of effort and difficulty effects on decision parameters.


## Conclusions

This chapter provides mechanistic evidence that the clearest supported locus of effort-induced interference in older adults is the quality of perceptual evidence accumulation. The DDM decomposition localizes the 40% MVC handgrip cost to the drift rate parameter $v$ — the signal-to-noise ratio of evidence integration — with a clear, credible interval excluding zero. The evidence hierarchy is as follows. First and strongest: drift rate was reliably reduced under High effort, with a posterior that consistently excluded zero. Second: boundary separation and starting-point bias showed near-zero effort contrasts with 95% CrIs spanning zero, providing no comparable positive evidence for compensatory caution adjustment or pre-stimulus criterion resetting; while these are graded rather than definitive nulls, they are inconsistent with a strong form of the strategic-adaptation account. Third and most uncertain: non-decision time could not be tested in the primary model due to the response-signal design constraint, and the exploratory estimate was too imprecise to support conclusions in either direction; pupil-linked mechanisms remain inconclusive due to PSIS-LOO unreliability and likely TEPR measurement confounds under sustained grip. These findings set the stage for Chapter 4, which directly tests whether locus coeruleus–norepinephrine (LC-NE) integrity — quantified via neuromelanin-sensitive MRI — moderates the effort-induced drift rate reduction observed here, and whether individuals with higher LC integrity are buffered against the perceptual costs of high physical demand.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ndt-prior-posterior

The prior is Normal(log(0.35), 0.15) on the log scale (approximately 0.35 s on natural scale). This figure documents prior influence for the response-signal design, where $t_0$ primarily reflects motor execution rather than encoding time."
#| fig-align: center

# Dynamic: from model in run_dir when brms available
model_path <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "models", "additive__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds")
if (file.exists(model_path) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tryCatch({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(brms); library(posterior) })
    fit_ndt <- readRDS(model_path)
    draws <- as_draws_df(fit_ndt, variable = "^b_ndt_", regex = TRUE)
    if (ncol(draws) > 0 && "b_ndt_Intercept" %in% names(draws)) {
      ndt_draws <- draws %>% pull(b_ndt_Intercept)
      ndt_prior <- tibble(x_log = seq(log(0.1), log(0.6), length.out = 400),
                          d = dnorm(x_log, mean = log(0.35), sd = 0.15), type = "Prior") %>%
        mutate(x_natural = exp(x_log))
      post_df <- tibble(x_log = as.numeric(ndt_draws)) %>%
        mutate(x_natural = exp(x_log), type = "Posterior")
      p_ndt <- ggplot() +
        geom_line(data = ndt_prior, aes(x = x_natural, y = d, color = "Prior"), alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.8) +
        geom_density(data = post_df, aes(x = x_natural, color = "Posterior", fill = "Posterior"), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.3) +
        scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Prior" = "gray50", "Posterior" = "steelblue")) +
        scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Posterior" = "steelblue"), guide = "none") +
        labs(x = "t0 (s)", y = "Density", title = "NDT Intercept: Prior vs Posterior",
             subtitle = "Prior: Normal(log(0.35), 0.15) on log scale") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top")
      print(p_ndt)
    } else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ndt_prior_posterior.pdf"))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ndt_prior_posterior.pdf"))
  })
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ndt_prior_posterior.pdf"))
}
```

## A2. Individual Differences and Parameter Relationships {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: fig-subject-parameter-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Subject-Level Parameter Distribution. Violin plots showing the distribution of subject-level random effects (deviations from group mean) for each DDM parameter. The boxplots within each violin show the median and interquartile range. Zero (dashed line) represents the group mean. This visualization highlights the substantial individual variability in decision-making parameters across our sample of 67 older adults."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "75%"
# Dynamic: from model ranef when brms available
model_path_re <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "models", "additive__probe_onset_locked__thr0.20.rds")
if (file.exists(model_path_re) && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  tryCatch({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(brms))
    fit_re <- readRDS(model_path_re)
    re <- ranef(fit_re)
    if (!is.null(re) && "subject_id" %in% names(re)) {
      re_subj <- re$subject_id
      par_names <- dimnames(re_subj)[[3]]
      re_list <- list()
      for (par in par_names) {
        if ("Estimate" %in% dimnames(re_subj)[[2]]) {
          re_est <- re_subj[, "Estimate", par]
          re_list[[length(re_list) + 1]] <- tibble(subject_id = names(re_est), parameter = par, estimate = as.numeric(re_est))
        }
      }
      if (length(re_list) > 0) {
      re_df <- bind_rows(re_list) %>%
        mutate(
          parameter = case_when(
            parameter == "Intercept" | (grepl("Intercept", parameter) & !grepl("bias|bs|ndt", parameter)) ~ "Drift (v)",
            grepl("bs_|boundary", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Boundary (a)",
            grepl("bias", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Bias (z)",
            grepl("ndt", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Non-decision time (t0)",
            TRUE ~ parameter
          )
        )
      re_df$parameter <- factor(re_df$parameter, levels = c("Drift (v)", "Boundary (a)", "Bias (z)", "Non-decision time (t0)"))
      re_df <- re_df %>% filter(!is.na(parameter))
      if (nrow(re_df) > 0) {
        p_re <- ggplot(re_df, aes(x = parameter, y = estimate, fill = parameter)) +
          geom_violin(alpha = 0.3, trim = FALSE) +
          geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
          geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
          scale_fill_manual(values = c("Drift (v)" = "#2E86AB", "Boundary (a)" = "#A23B72", "Bias (z)" = "#28A745", "Non-decision time (t0)" = "#6C757D"), guide = "none") +
          labs(title = "Subject-Level Parameter Estimates (Random Effects)", subtitle = "Individual differences in DDM parameters",
               x = "DDM Parameter", y = "Random Effect Estimate (link scale)", fill = "Parameter") +
          theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
        print(p_re)
      } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_subject_parameter_distribution.pdf")) }
      } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_subject_parameter_distribution.pdf")) }
    } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_subject_parameter_distribution.pdf")) }
  }, error = function(e) { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_subject_parameter_distribution.pdf")) })
} else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_subject_parameter_distribution.pdf"))
}
```

```{r}
          theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray50"))
        print(p_cor)
      } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("plot4_parameter_correlation.png")) }
    } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("plot4_parameter_correlation.png")) }
  }, error = function(e) { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("plot4_parameter_correlation.png")) })
} else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("plot4_parameter_correlation.png"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-brinley-plot
#| fig-cap: "Brinley Plot: Reaction Time Relationships. Scatter plot showing mean RT for Hard trials (y-axis) versus Easy trials (x-axis) for each participant, colored by effort condition (blue = Low effort, crimson = High effort). Reaction times are displayed in milliseconds (ms). The dashed diagonal line (slope = 1) represents proportional slowing (equal RT increase in both conditions). The solid black regression line shows the actual relationship with 95% confidence interval (shaded ribbon), with slope > 1 indicating disproportionate slowing in Hard trials relative to Easy trials. Points above the diagonal indicate participants who slowed more in Hard relative to Easy trials. This visualization connects our DDM findings to the broader cognitive aging literature on generalized slowing [@brinley1965cognitive; @cerella1985; @salthouse1996]."
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "70%"
# Dynamic: computed from behavioral_data
if (!is.null(behavioral_data) && nrow(behavioral_data) > 0) {
  subj_col <- intersect(c("subject_id", "sub"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  rt_col <- intersect(c("rt", "same_diff_resp_secs", "resp1RT"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  diff_col <- intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  effort_col <- intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(subj_col) && !is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)) {
    brinley_data <- behavioral_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0, !!sym(rt_col) < 10,
             !is.na(!!sym(diff_col)), !is.na(!!sym(effort_col))) %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
      summarise(mean_rt = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = !!sym(diff_col), values_from = mean_rt, names_prefix = "mean_rt_")
    if ("mean_rt_Easy" %in% names(brinley_data) && "mean_rt_Hard" %in% names(brinley_data)) {
      brinley_plot_data <- brinley_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(mean_rt_Easy), !is.na(mean_rt_Hard)) %>%
        mutate(
          mean_rt_Easy_ms = mean_rt_Easy * 1000,
          mean_rt_Hard_ms = mean_rt_Hard * 1000,
          effort = !!sym(effort_col)
        )
      effort_levs <- unique(brinley_plot_data$effort)
      high_eff <- effort_levs[grepl("High|40", as.character(effort_levs), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
      low_eff  <- effort_levs[grepl("Low|5", as.character(effort_levs), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
      if (is.na(high_eff)) high_eff <- effort_levs[1]
      if (is.na(low_eff))  low_eff <- effort_levs[length(effort_levs)]
      color_map <- setNames(c("#DC143C", "#1E90FF"), c(as.character(high_eff), as.character(low_eff)))
      fit_line <- lm(mean_rt_Hard_ms ~ mean_rt_Easy_ms, data = brinley_plot_data)
      slope <- coef(fit_line)[2]
      p_brinley <- ggplot(brinley_plot_data, aes(x = mean_rt_Easy_ms, y = mean_rt_Hard_ms)) +
        geom_point(aes(color = effort), size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
        geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.2) +
        scale_color_manual(values = color_map, labels = c("High Effort", "Low Effort")) +
        labs(title = "Brinley Plot: Reaction Time Relationships",
             subtitle = sprintf("Easy vs. Hard difficulty (slope = %.2f)", slope),
             x = "Mean RT: Easy Trials (ms)", y = "Mean RT: Hard Trials (ms)", color = "Effort Condition") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray60"),
              legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      print(p_brinley)
    } else {
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
    }
  } else {
    include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
  }
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_brinley_plot.pdf"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bias-drift-intercept
#| tbl-cap: "Drift intercept (Standard-only model)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
if (!is.null(tbl_sob_fixef)) {
  if ("rt_def" %in% names(tbl_sob_fixef) && !"rt_type" %in% names(tbl_sob_fixef)) {
    tbl_sob_fixef <- tbl_sob_fixef %>% rename(rt_type = rt_def)
  }
  drift_intercept_raw <- tbl_sob_fixef %>%
    filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT) %>%
    filter(term == "Intercept" | term == "(Intercept)") %>%
    filter(!grepl("^bias_|^bs_|^ndt_|^b_", term, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    { if ("dpar" %in% names(.)) filter(., dpar == "v") else . } %>%
    slice(1)
  if (nrow(drift_intercept_raw) > 0) {
    est_col <- if ("Estimate" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Estimate" else "estimate"
    q2_col <- if ("Q2.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Q2.5" else if ("q2.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "q2.5" else NA_character_
    q97_col <- if ("Q97.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Q97.5" else if ("q97.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "q97.5" else NA_character_
    if (is.na(q2_col) || is.na(q97_col)) {
      tibble(Note = "CI columns not found in standard_only_bias_fixef_link_scale.csv.") %>%
        knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
    } else {
      drift_intercept <- drift_intercept_raw %>%
        select(!!sym(est_col), !!sym(q2_col), !!sym(q97_col)) %>%
        mutate(
          estimate = round(!!sym(est_col), 3),
          q2.5 = round(!!sym(q2_col), 3),
          q97.5 = round(!!sym(q97_col), 3),
          `95% CrI` = paste0("[", q2.5, ", ", q97.5, "]")
        ) %>%
        select(estimate, `95% CrI`) %>%
        rename(`Estimate` = estimate)
      drift_intercept %>%
        knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), full_width = FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    tibble(Note = "Drift intercept not found in standard_only_bias_fixef_link_scale.csv.") %>%
      knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  tibble(Note = "Data not available for drift intercept table.") %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
}
```

## A3. Posterior Predictive Checks and Diagnostics {#app-ch3-ppc .unnumbered}

Table 16 summarizes convergence and PPC diagnostic metrics for the primary model; convergence criteria were strictly satisfied (PASS) while PPC threshold exceedances were driven by fast-tail misfit as discussed below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-convergence-ppc-gate-appendix
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence and PPC Diagnostics (Primary Model). Convergence criteria (R-hat, ESS, divergences) were strictly satisfied (PASS). PPC metrics show exceedances of pre-registered strict thresholds, driven by fast-tail misfit — a known limitation of standard Wiener DDM without fast-guess processes. These PPC threshold failures do not invalidate parameter contrasts; visual diagnostics (QP plots, Appendix A3.2) confirmed adequate mid-body fit, and key contrasts were robust to tail deviations. Note: 'Convergence verdict' and 'PPC verdict' reflect different standards — convergence is a binary prerequisite for valid inference; PPC threshold failures indicate model limitations but do not prevent interpretation. See Section 3.2 and Appendix A3 for full discussion."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Prefer run_dir convergence (matches main DDM data); fallback to publish_gate for conv and PPC
conv_primary_row <- tbl_convergence %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  slice(1)
conv_max_rhat   <- if (nrow(conv_primary_row) > 0) conv_primary_row$max_rhat   else (if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$conv_max_rhat   else NA_real_)
conv_min_bulk   <- if (nrow(conv_primary_row) > 0) conv_primary_row$min_bulk_ess else (if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$conv_min_bulk_ess else NA_real_)
conv_min_tail   <- if (!is.null(publish_gate) && !is.na(publish_gate$conv_min_tail_ess)) publish_gate$conv_min_tail_ess else NA_real_  # run_dir has no tail ESS
conv_div        <- if (nrow(conv_primary_row) > 0) conv_primary_row$n_divergent else (if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$conv_divergences else NA_integer_)
conv_pass       <- !is.na(conv_max_rhat) && conv_max_rhat < 1.01 && !is.na(conv_min_bulk) && conv_min_bulk >= 400 && !is.na(conv_div) && conv_div == 0
ppc_n_cells     <- if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$ppc_subj_n_cells     else NA_real_
ppc_pct_flagged <- if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$ppc_subj_pct_flagged_any else NA_real_
ppc_max_qp      <- if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$ppc_subj_max_qp     else NA_real_
ppc_max_ks      <- if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$ppc_subj_max_ks      else NA_real_
ppc_pass        <- if (!is.null(publish_gate)) publish_gate$ppc_subj_pass        else NA
if (!is.null(publish_gate) || nrow(conv_primary_row) > 0) {
  gate_tbl <- tibble(
    Metric = c(
      "Max R-hat", "Min Bulk ESS", "Min Tail ESS", "Divergences",
      "Convergence verdict", "PPC Cells (n)", "PPC Flagged (%)",
      "Max QP RMSE (s)", "Max KS", "PPC verdict"
    ),
    Value = c(
      ifelse(is.na(conv_max_rhat), "—", sprintf("%.4f", conv_max_rhat)),
      ifelse(is.na(conv_min_bulk), "—", sprintf("%.0f", conv_min_bulk)),
      ifelse(is.na(conv_min_tail), "—", sprintf("%.0f", conv_min_tail)),
      as.character(ifelse(is.na(conv_div), "—", conv_div)),
      ifelse(is.na(conv_pass), "—", ifelse(conv_pass, "PASS (Rhat ≤ 1.01, ESS ≥ 400, 0 divergences)", "FAIL")),
      ifelse(is.na(ppc_n_cells), "—", sprintf("%.0f", ppc_n_cells)),
      ifelse(is.na(ppc_pct_flagged), "—", sprintf("%.1f%%", ppc_pct_flagged)),
      ifelse(is.na(ppc_max_qp), "—", sprintf("%.3f", ppc_max_qp)),
      ifelse(is.na(ppc_max_ks), "—", sprintf("%.3f", ppc_max_ks)),
      ifelse(is.na(ppc_pass), "—", ifelse(ppc_pass, "PASS strict thresholds", "FAIL pre-registered thresholds (fast-tail driven; mid-body fit adequate, inferences robust)"))
    )
  )
  gate_tbl %>% gt() %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_column_labels()) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(style = "italic"), locations = cells_body(columns = Metric)) %>%
    cols_width(Metric ~ px(180), Value ~ px(100)) %>% opt_table_font(size = "small")
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

**Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF).** The Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF) shows how accuracy varies across RT bins, providing a diagnostic for speed–accuracy tradeoffs. @fig-caf plots empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Consistent with evidence-accumulation dynamics, faster responses (lower RT bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy. This pattern validates the DDM's core assumption that decisions improve with longer evidence accumulation times.

```{r}
#| label: fig-caf
#| fig-cap: "Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF). Empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Shows the speed–accuracy tradeoff: faster responses (lower bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy, consistent with evidence accumulation over time."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "85%"
# Dynamic: prefer behavioral_data (fresh on re-render), else load 04_all_caf_empirical.csv
caf_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output/publish/04_all_caf_empirical.csv")
caf_from_behav <- !is.null(behavioral_data) && nrow(behavioral_data) > 0
rt_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("rt", "same_diff_resp_secs", "resp1RT"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
acc_col_behav <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("correct", "iscorr", "accuracy", "resp_is_correct"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
task_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("task", "Task"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
diff_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("difficulty_level", "difficulty"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
effort_col <- if (caf_from_behav) intersect(c("effort_condition", "effort"), names(behavioral_data))[1] else NULL
caf_from_behav <- caf_from_behav && !is.null(rt_col) && !is.null(acc_col_behav) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)

if (caf_from_behav) {
  caf_computed <- behavioral_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0, !!sym(rt_col) < 10,
           !is.na(!!sym(acc_col_behav)), !is.na(!!sym(task_col)), !is.na(!!sym(diff_col)), !is.na(!!sym(effort_col))) %>%
    mutate(
      task = factor(!!sym(task_col)),
      effort_condition = factor(case_when(grepl("High|40", as.character(!!sym(effort_col))) ~ "High", TRUE ~ "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High")),
      difficulty_level = factor(!!sym(diff_col), levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard"))
    ) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition, difficulty_level) %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(!!sym(rt_col), breaks = 5, labels = FALSE)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(bin)) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition, difficulty_level, bin) %>%
    summarise(acc_emp = mean(as.numeric(!!sym(acc_col_behav)), na.rm = TRUE), bin_rt_mid = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(caf_computed) > 0) {
    p_caf <- ggplot(caf_computed, aes(x = bin_rt_mid, y = acc_emp)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.1, color = "black") + geom_path(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
      facet_grid(task + effort_condition ~ difficulty_level) +
      labs(x = "RT bin midpoint (s)", y = "Accuracy", title = "Conditional Accuracy Function: Accuracy by RT Bin",
           subtitle = "Empirical accuracy (speed-accuracy tradeoff)") +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
    print(p_caf)
  } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
} else if (file.exists(caf_file)) {
  caf_data <- read_csv(caf_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  acc_col <- intersect(c("acc_emp", "emp_caf"), names(caf_data))[1]
  bin_col <- intersect(c("bin_rt_mid", "bin"), names(caf_data))[1]
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(bin_col)) {
    if (acc_col == "emp_caf") caf_data <- caf_data %>% rename(acc_emp = emp_caf)
    caf_plot <- caf_data %>%
      mutate(
        task = factor(task),
        effort_condition = factor(case_when(grepl("High|40", as.character(effort_condition)) ~ "High", TRUE ~ "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High")),
        difficulty_level = factor(difficulty_level, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
        bin_rt_mid = as.numeric(!!sym(bin_col))
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(acc_emp), is.finite(acc_emp))
    if (nrow(caf_plot) > 0) {
      p_caf <- ggplot(caf_plot, aes(x = bin_rt_mid, y = acc_emp)) +
        geom_point(size = 1.1, color = "black") + geom_path(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
        facet_grid(task + effort_condition ~ difficulty_level) +
        labs(x = "RT bin midpoint (s)", y = "Accuracy", title = "Conditional Accuracy Function: Accuracy by RT Bin",
             subtitle = "Empirical accuracy (speed-accuracy tradeoff)") +
        scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "gray50", hjust = 0.5), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
      print(p_caf)
    } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
  } else { include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf")) }
} else {
  include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf"))
}
```

**PPC Residual Heatmaps.** PPC residual heatmaps visualize model fit across the 12 experimental cells (Task × Effort × Difficulty). Each cell is colored by two fit metrics: KS statistic (Kolmogorov–Smirnov, comparing RT distributions) and QP RMSE (quantile–probability root-mean-squared error, comparing RT quantiles). Darker red indicates poorer fit. Pre-declared thresholds were KS $<$ 0.15 (warn) and $<$ 0.20 (fail), QP RMSE $<$ 0.09 s (warn) and $<$ 0.12 s (fail). Most cells show acceptable fit (light colors), with notable misfit concentrated in Easy–VDT conditions (darker red), consistent with known fast-tail underfitting in the base Wiener DDM.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-heatmaps
#| fig-cap: "PPC Residual Heatmaps. KS statistic and QP RMSE by Task × Effort × Difficulty for all models (top panel) and primary model only (bottom panel). Darker red indicates larger residuals (poorer fit). The primary model shows acceptable fit across most cells, with notable misfit in Easy/VDT conditions."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "80%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ppc_heatmaps.pdf"))
```

## A4. Sensitivity Analyses {.unnumbered}

### A4.1 Exclusion of Sub-Chance Participants {.unnumbered}

To verify that the inclusion of 12 participants who performed at or near chance ($\leq$ 55% accuracy, compared to 50% two-alternative forced-choice baseline) in some conditions did not bias our main findings, we conducted sensitivity analyses comparing the primary model (N=67) with models fit after excluding these participants (N=55).

**Method**: We refit the primary model (Model3_Difficulty) and an additive model (Model4_Additive) on the reduced dataset excluding sub-chance participants. Parameter estimates were compared using delta (sensitivity - baseline) with conservative 95% credible intervals. If the delta CI includes zero and the baseline and sensitivity CIs overlap, we conclude the parameter is robust to exclusion.

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity-subchance
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity Analysis: Excluding Sub-Chance Participants"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
#| echo: false
if (!is.null(sensitivity_summary) && exists("has_sensitivity_summary") && has_sensitivity_summary) {
  # Function to clean model names (reuse from LOO table)
  clean_model_name <- function(model) {
    model <- as.character(model)
    
    # Single parameter models
    model <- ifelse(model == "v", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z", "Difficulty → z (bias)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "a", "Difficulty → a (boundary)", model)
    
    # Two-parameter combinations
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z", "Difficulty → v + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a", "Difficulty → v + a", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z_a", "Difficulty → z + a", model)
    
    # Three-parameter combination
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z_a", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a_z", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    
    # Model number formats
    model <- gsub("Model3_Difficulty", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model4_Additive", "Additive (v + a + z)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model5_Interaction", "Interaction", model)
    model <- gsub("Model10_Param_v_bs", "v + a parameterized", model)
    
    # Remove common prefixes
    model <- gsub("^Difficulty_on_", "", model)
    model <- gsub("^difficulty_", "", model)
    
    # Format underscores as separators
    model <- gsub("_", " ", model)
    
    return(model)
  }
  
  # Function to clean parameter names (reuse from DDM parameter function)
  clean_ddm_parameter <- function(param) {
    param <- as.character(param)
    original <- param
    n <- length(param)
    result <- character(n)
    
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      p <- param[i]
      orig <- original[i]
      
      # Determine parameter type from prefix
      param_type <- ""
      if (grepl("^bs_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        p <- gsub("^bs_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^bias_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        p <- gsub("^bias_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^ndt_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        p <- gsub("^ndt_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^b_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Drift (v)"
        p <- gsub("^b_", "", p)
      } else {
        # Try to infer from content
        if (grepl("bs|boundary", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        } else if (grepl("ndt|non.decision", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        } else if (grepl("bias", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        } else {
          param_type <- "Drift (v)"  # Default
        }
      }
      
      # Handle Intercept
      if (p == "Intercept" || orig == "Intercept") {
        result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": Intercept")
        next
      }
      
      # Handle task-specific parameters that are already formatted (e.g., "Drift (v): ADT")
      # These come from the updated extraction script that computes task-specific intercepts
      if (grepl(": (ADT|VDT)$", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        result[i] <- orig  # Pass through already-formatted task-specific parameters
        next
      }
      
      # Step 1: Check if this is an interaction (has colon between different factors in raw R format)
      # Interactions have colons between factor patterns like difficulty_level:task or effort_condition:task
      is_raw_interaction <- grepl("_level:", p) || grepl("_condition:", p) || 
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("effort_condition", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":effort_condition", p))
      
      if (is_raw_interaction) {
        # Handle interactions: split by colon between factors, clean each part, join with ×
        # Pattern: difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT -> split -> clean -> "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT"
        if (grepl(":", p) && !grepl(" × ", p)) {
          # Split by colon (assuming only one colon between factors for interactions)
          parts <- strsplit(p, ":")[[1]]
          # Clean each part
          cleaned_parts <- character(length(parts))
          for (j in seq_along(parts)) {
            part <- parts[j]
            # Clean difficulty
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean task
            part <- gsub("^taskVDT$", "Task: VDT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^taskADT$", "Task: ADT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean effort
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_MVC$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_MVC$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            cleaned_parts[j] <- part
          }
          # Join with ×
          p <- paste(cleaned_parts, collapse = " × ")
        }
      } else {
        # Step 2: Main effects - clean normally (preserve colons)
      # Clean difficulty levels (flexible matching)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean task
      p <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean effort conditions (handle all variations - order matters!)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_MVC", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      }
      
      # Add parameter type prefix if we have meaningful content
      if (p != orig && param_type != "") {
        # Check if param already starts with a parameter type (avoid duplication)
        if (!grepl("^(Drift|Boundary|Non-decision|Bias)", p)) {
          result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": ", p)
        } else {
          result[i] <- p
        }
      } else {
        result[i] <- p
      }
    }
    
    return(result)
  }
  
  sens_subchance <- sensitivity_summary %>%
    filter(sensitivity == "exclude_subchance") %>%
    mutate(
      model_clean = clean_model_name(model),
      parameter_clean = clean_ddm_parameter(parameter),
      across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    select(model_clean, parameter_clean, baseline_estimate, sensitivity_estimate, delta, 
           delta_ci_lower, delta_ci_upper, ci_overlap, delta_contains_zero) %>%
    rename(model = model_clean, parameter = parameter_clean) %>%
    mutate(model = case_when(
      model == "Additive model" ~ "Additive model",
      model == "Baseline model" ~ "Baseline model",
      TRUE ~ model
    )) %>%
    arrange(model, parameter)
  
  if (nrow(sens_subchance) > 0) {
    sens_subchance %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        model = dplyr::recode(
          model,
          "additive" = "Additive (v + a + z)",
          "Additive v a z" = "Additive (v + a + z)",
          "baseline" = "Baseline (intercept-only)",
          "difficulty" = "Difficulty-only (no Effort)",
          "Difficulty v drift" = "Difficulty-only (no Effort)"
        )
      ) %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        model = "Model",
        parameter = "Parameter",
        baseline_estimate = "Baseline",
        sensitivity_estimate = "Excluded",
        delta = "Δ",
        delta_ci_lower = "Δ CI Lower",
        delta_ci_upper = "Δ CI Upper",
        ci_overlap = "CI Overlap",
        delta_contains_zero = "Δ Contains 0"
      ) %>%
      tab_footnote(
        footnote = "Baseline: N=67 (includes sub-chance). Excluded: N=55 (excludes sub-chance). Δ = Excluded - Baseline. If Δ CI contains 0 and CIs overlap, parameter is robust.",
        locations = cells_column_labels(columns = delta_contains_zero)
      ) %>%
      tab_source_note(
        source_note = "Parameter estimates are posterior medians; Δ CI is the 95% credible interval for the difference between the full sample and the sub-chance-excluded subsample."
      ) %>%
      opt_table_font(size = "small") %>%
      tab_options(
        table.width = pct(90),
        table.font.size = px(9),
        column_labels.font.size = px(10),
        column_labels.padding = px(8),
        data_row.padding = px(6),
        table_body.hlines.width = px(0.5),
        table_body.vlines.width = px(0.5),
        table.border.top.width = px(1.5),
        table.border.bottom.width = px(1.5)
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      )
  } else {
    tibble(Note = "No sensitivity data available.") %>%
      knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE) %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  tibble(Note = "Sensitivity summary data not loaded.") %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", full_width = FALSE)
}
```

```{=latex}
\end{landscape}
```

**Results**: Most key parameters showed robust estimates when excluding sub-chance participants. For Model3_Difficulty and Model4_Additive, the drift intercept and boundary separation showed delta CIs that included zero, indicating no meaningful change. The Easy difficulty effect was also robust. The Hard difficulty effect showed a small shift ($\Delta \approx -0.10$, delta CI did not include zero), but this represents a small change in magnitude (approximately 6.5% of the baseline estimate) and does not alter the substantive conclusion that Hard trials show negative drift relative to Standard. 

**Conclusion**: Sensitivity analyses confirmed that inclusion of these participants did not alter the pattern of main effects. The inclusion of sub-chance participants did not meaningfully alter main effects or substantive conclusions, supporting our decision to retain all 67 participants to maximize sample size and leverage hierarchical modeling's ability to stabilize estimates through shrinkage.

### A4.2 RT Cutoff Thresholds {.unnumbered}

The difficulty gradient (Easy > Hard > Standard) and the effort effect on drift rate were preserved across all three RT cutoff thresholds (see @tbl-app-sensitivity-full and the figures below for full parameter estimates and plots), confirming that the primary findings are not sensitive to the choice of RT lower bound.

Because different RT cutoffs exclude different numbers of trials, raw LOOIC values are **not directly comparable** across thresholds (@tbl-sensitivity-thresholds). LOOIC is a measure of total log predictive density, which scales with sample size. We therefore evaluate sensitivity by comparing **parameter estimates** and **effect directions** across cutoffs, not by selecting the "best" LOOIC model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity-thresholds
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity to minimum cue-locked RT cutoff (0.15/0.20/0.25 s)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build sensitivity table from tbl_sens (handle optional LOOIC columns)
# Build column list dynamically
cols_to_select <- c("threshold", "n_trials")
if ("looic" %in% names(tbl_sens)) {
  cols_to_select <- c(cols_to_select, "looic")
}
if ("looic_se" %in% names(tbl_sens)) {
  cols_to_select <- c(cols_to_select, "looic_se")
}

tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens %>%
  select(all_of(cols_to_select)) %>%
  arrange(threshold)

# Add LOOIC columns if they don't exist
if (!"looic" %in% names(tbl_sens_base)) {
  tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens_base %>% mutate(looic = NA_real_)
}
if (!"looic_se" %in% names(tbl_sens_base)) {
  tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens_base %>% mutate(looic_se = NA_real_)
}

tbl_sens_compact <- tbl_sens_base %>%
  mutate(
    looic = if (!all(is.na(looic))) round(looic, 1) else NA_real_,
    looic_se = if (!all(is.na(looic_se))) round(looic_se, 1) else NA_real_,
    n_trials = format(n_trials, big.mark = ",")
  ) %>%
  select(threshold, n_trials, looic, looic_se) %>%
  rename(
    `Threshold (s)` = threshold,
    `N trials` = n_trials,
    `LOOIC` = looic,
    `LOOIC SE` = looic_se
  )

tbl_sens_compact %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

We adopted 0.20 s as the primary cutoff, balancing exclusion of fast guesses with trial retention (@tbl-sensitivity-thresholds); all subsequent reported effects refer to this threshold.

```{r}
if (!is.null(tbl_sens) && nrow(tbl_sens) > 0) {

    arrange(threshold) %>%

      across(where(is.numeric) & !matches("threshold"), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
                 booktabs = TRUE,

    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "scale_down"),
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
} else {

}
```

### A4.3 Task Modality Effects: Sensitivity Analysis {.unnumbered}

The primary model (Table 8) excluded Task (ADT vs. VDT) as a predictor for drift rate ($v$) and boundary separation ($a$) to reduce model complexity. We additionally examined whether absolute drift rates differed between auditory and visual tasks, as pooling these modalities could potentially mask Task main effects or Effort × Task interactions. To address this, we fit a **task-sensitivity model** with:

- Drift rate ($v$): `~ difficulty + effort * task` (with interaction)
- Boundary separation ($a$): `~ difficulty + effort + task` (main effects only)
- All other parameters unchanged from the primary model

#### Drift Rate by Task {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: fig-suppl-drift-by-task
#| fig-cap: "**Supplementary Figure 1.** Drift rate ($v$) by difficulty and effort, separately for ADT and VDT. Points show posterior medians with 95% credible intervals. The difficulty gradient (Standard $<$ Hard $<$ Easy) is consistent across tasks. High effort reduces drift rate in both modalities (no significant Effort $\\times$ Task interaction), confirming that cognitive-motor interference generalizes across sensory domains. *Note: Drift rates ($v$) were estimated using Response Coding. Positive values indicate evidence accumulation toward the 'Different' boundary; negative values indicate accumulation toward the 'Same' boundary.*"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-pos: "htbp"
#| out-width: "75%"

drift_plot_data_suppl <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT"))
  )
if ("drift_estimate" %in% names(drift_plot_data_suppl)) {
  drift_plot_data_suppl <- drift_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(drift_val = drift_estimate, drift_lower = if ("drift_low" %in% names(.)) drift_low else drift_q2.5, drift_upper = if ("drift_high" %in% names(.)) drift_high else drift_q97.5)
} else {
  drift_plot_data_suppl <- drift_plot_data_suppl %>%
    mutate(drift_val = drift_median, drift_lower = drift_q2.5, drift_upper = drift_q97.5)
}

p_drift_cond <- ggplot(drift_plot_data_suppl, aes(x = difficulty, y = drift_val, color = effort, group = effort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = drift_lower, ymax = drift_upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ task, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  labs(x = "Difficulty", y = "Drift Rate (v)", title = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)

print(p_drift_cond)
```

#### Task-Sensitivity Model Comparison {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-task-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of Effort Effects: Primary vs. Task-Sensitivity Model"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
task_sens_path <- file.path(proj_root, params$run_dir, "tables", "task_sensitivity_comparison.csv")
if (file.exists(task_sens_path)) {
  task_sens_comp <- read_csv(task_sens_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  task_sens_comp %>%
    mutate(
      `95% CrI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", CI_lower, CI_upper),
      Estimate = sprintf("%.3f", Estimate)
    ) %>%
    select(Parameter, Estimate, `95% CrI`) %>%
    knitr::kable(booktabs = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position") %>%
    kableExtra::add_footnote(
      "Note. Primary model excludes Task from drift; Task-Sens model includes Task main effect and Effort×Task interaction.",
      notation = "none"
    )
} else {
  cat("Task-sensitivity comparison table not yet available. Run the full DDM refit pipeline to generate it.")
}
```

The task-sensitivity model confirmed that the Effort → Drift effect was robust to inclusion of Task modality as a predictor ($\delta \approx -0.085$, 95% CrI $[-0.133, -0.038]$; same direction and credibility as the primary model). A credible Task main effect was observed ($\delta \approx 0.071$, 95% CrI $[0.020, 0.120]$), indicating that auditory and visual tasks differed modestly in absolute drift rates. However, the Effort $\times$ Task interaction was negligible ($\delta \approx 0.029$, 95% CrI $[-0.029, 0.088]$), confirming that cognitive-motor interference under High effort manifested similarly across sensory modalities. These results support the primary model's decision to pool ADT and VDT for main analyses, and validate the generalizability of the core drift rate finding across stimulus modalities.

```{r pdf-sanity-check}
#| include: false
#| eval: false
# Post-render PDF sanity check: verify no unresolved crossrefs remain
# To enable: change eval to true (or run manually after rendering)
# Requires: pdftotext (part of poppler-utils package)
# 
# This check prevents accidentally distributing PDFs with broken crossrefs.
# If any unresolved refs are found, the build will fail with a clear error message.

pdf_file <- "chap3_ddm_results.pdf"

if (file.exists(pdf_file)) {
  # Extract text from PDF
  pdf_text <- system2("pdftotext", args = c(pdf_file, "-"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  
  # Check for unresolved crossrefs
  unresolved_patterns <- c(
    "Table \\?\\?",
    "Figure \\?\\?",
    "\\?@fig-",
    "\\?@tbl-",
    "\\?@sec-"
  )
  
  matches <- character(0)
  for (pattern in unresolved_patterns) {
    pattern_matches <- grep(pattern, pdf_text, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
    if (length(pattern_matches) > 0) {
      matches <- c(matches, pattern_matches)
    }
  }
  
  if (length(matches) > 0) {
    cat("ERROR: Unresolved crossrefs found in PDF:\n\n")
    for (match in unique(matches)) {
      cat("  ", match, "\n")
    }
    cat("\nFix the broken references above before distributing the PDF.\n")
    stop("Unresolved crossrefs remain in PDF. Build failed.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    cat("✓ PDF sanity check PASSED: No unresolved crossrefs found.\n")
  }
} else {
  warning("PDF file not found: ", pdf_file, ". Run this check after rendering.")
}
```


## A5. Pupil-DDM Fixed Effects (Link Scale) {#app-pupil-fixef .unnumbered}

Full parameter tables for the pupil-linked DDM confirm that global TEPR effects on drift rate and starting-point bias were near zero (posterior means near zero, 95% CrIs including zero; @tbl-pupil-key-effects). PSIS-LOO comparisons in Section 3.6 did not show **reliable** predictive differences versus the behavioral baseline: Pareto-$k$ diagnostics (max $k$ = 0.91) indicate PSIS-LOO estimates are unreliable, so conclusions rest on posterior coefficient distributions rather than ELPD rankings. The primary inferential figure is @fig-pupil-drift-difficulty-interaction, which shows difficulty-conditional posterior slopes of `pupil_scaled` on drift rate from the `pupil_scaled * difficulty` interaction model. Complete coefficient tables are available in the online supplement at [https://github.com/mohdasti/modeling-pupil-DDM](https://github.com/mohdasti/modeling-pupil-DDM).
